columns.bill_id: The bill this action belongs to.
columns.action_index: Zero-based position in the publisher's own action list, which runs newest first: 0 is the bill's latest action. Part of the identity.
columns.action_date: The publisher's actionDate for this action.
columns.action_time: The publisher's actionTime, where the source system states one.
columns.action_text: The action text exactly as written, whitespace included; NULL when the publisher stated none.
columns.action_code: The publisher's action code, which is what the became-law rule keys on.
columns.action_type: The publisher's action type (IntroReferral, Floor, BecameLaw...).
columns.source_system_name: Name of the system that reported the action.
columns.recorded_vote_count: How many recordedVote entries this action carries.
columns.is_latest_action: True on the one actions[] entry the publisher's separate latestAction element names.
columns.stage: The stage this one action's qualified code and text classify as, in the same vocabulary as congress_bills.stage (`introduced`, `committee`, `calendared`, `passed_chamber`, `other_chamber`, `conference`, `cleared`, `presented`, `law`, or the outcomes `failed` and `vetoed`; never `passed_both`, which is a bill's state, not one action's); `introduced` with stage_rule NULL when no rule classifies the action, as for the desk or a floor step in the bill's own chamber. An action reads `cleared` where its own words complete agreement on one text; a chamber's agreement to a conference report reads `conference` here, and the bill reads `cleared` from the second, or from its listed enrolled text, which no action reads. One action's classification, not the bill's state.
columns.action_committees: Ordered committee references stated on this action. NULL means the source omitted the group. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.action_calendar_numbers: Calendar references stated on this action, without inheriting bill-level calendars. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.action_recorded_votes: Ordered recorded-vote references the publisher attached to this action. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.source_page_sha256: Exact Congress.gov API child-page digest, when the action came from that route.
columns.source_page_observed_at: When the child page was captured, independent of the parent observation and action date.
columns.source_page_row_index: Zero-based position of the action in its retained API page.

columns.document_key: The stating document's own natural key in its family's spelling; the GovInfo `packageId` for a package.  Spelled exactly as `document_citations.document_key`, so the two tables join.
columns.document_kind: Which family the stating document belongs to, so one table serves all of them.
columns.bill_id: `congress_bills.bill_id` for the measure this action is attached to, in the citation rule's own spelling.  The Congress is the one the document says it covers (`house_activity_reports.covered_congress`), unless the print states the bill's own -- set right after it (`H.R. 6752, 115th Cong.`) or in a Congress subheading over it -- because a print mostly writes `H.R. 1093` with no Congress beside it; a bill the document states no Congress for has no `bill_id` and attaches no action.  `house_activity_reports.bills_congress_mismatch` counts the bills the MODS keys under another Congress.
columns.print_phrasing: What the print wrote, from the sealed additions-only vocabulary in `interpretation.bill_actions.PRINT_ACTION_RULES` -- `held_hearing`, `ordered_reported`, `favorably_forwarded`, `declined_markup` and 21 others.  It names the *phrasing*, never the legislative event: the event is `sealed_stage`, and a phrasing with no rung keeps its own name rather than being given an invented code.  Additions-only because this value is published: a renamed key rewrites rows that are already out.
columns.span_start: Character offset of the **action phrase** in the document's normalized text, counted from zero, and part of the identity.  The phrase rather than the bill: one sentence states *signed by the President* and *became Public Law No: 118-83* about the same bill, which is two events' worth of evidence and two rows, and only the phrase offset tells them apart.
columns.span_end: Character offset just past the phrase, so `text[span_start:span_end]` is `matched_text`.
columns.matched_text: The exact characters the phrase rule matched, so a wrong row is readable without the document in hand.  The two measured classification failures both show up here: a `Pub. L.` cite naming the law a bill *amends*, and `reported to Congress` inside a bill's own subject matter.
columns.mention_span_start: Character offset of the bill designator this phrase was attached to.  Equal to a `document_citations.span_start` for the same document and digest, which is how a consumer walks from an action to the citation row that found the bill.
columns.mention_span_end: Character offset just past that designator.
columns.sentence_start: Character offset the sentence this was read in begins at, so a consumer can re-read the whole clause and judge the row.  The sentence is the unit because the *entry* is not one: this family writes a bill's long title as its own sentence and the disposition as the fragment after it, and every committee sets an entry differently.
columns.sentence_end: Character offset just past that sentence.
columns.bills_in_sentence: How many distinct bills that sentence names.  **This is the reliability predicate**, published as the raw count so a consumer can set its own threshold rather than trusting a label: `attachment_confidence` is derived from it and nothing else.
columns.sealed_stage: The rung of `interpretation.bill_stage`'s ladder this phrase resolves to, or NULL.  Derived by running the matched phrase through `infer_stage_from_text`, never asserted beside it.  NULL on 1,670 of 4,456 rows and that is a finding, not a gap: the print's register is not BILLSTATUS's.  `passed the House` is the sharpest case -- the sealed matcher is `passed house`, one word away -- and it is recorded NULL rather than closed by widening the sealed matcher list.
columns.billstatus_action_codes: The `<actionCode>` values the publisher uses for this phrasing in this row's chamber, joined; NULL where no code is known for it.  **Both kinds are not in the retained user guide.** A House committee hearing is coded `H21000` and a markup `H15000-B`, `H15001` or `H22000`, and none of the four appears in the guide's section 3 -- which states in its own first paragraph that it is representational and that no authoritative list exists.  They were read off the publisher's responses instead, and `interpretation.bill_actions.GuideCode.source` records which of the two a code came from, because only a guide-listed one can be checked against a committed fixture.  NULL on `favorably_forwarded`, `declined_markup`, `not_considered`, `included_in` and `vetoed` -- 280 rows -- where no code is known from either. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.chamber: Which chamber's vocabulary the codes were chosen from, read off the row and not off the document: a House committee's report states `the Senate passed H.R. 2365` and reports a Senate committee's action on a Senate bill, and both belong to the Senate side while sitting in a House print.  The phrase decides it where the phrase names a chamber, and the measure's own type otherwise.
columns.stated_date: The first date the sentence states, ISO, or NULL.  **Unscored**: the dates are extracted and published, and whether this one belongs to *this* action rather than to a neighbouring clause was never hand-checked.  `stated_date_count` says when the sentence stated more than one, which is when the attribution is least safe.
columns.stated_date_count: How many dates that sentence states.  Above one, `stated_date` is the first of several and a consumer wanting certainty re-reads the sentence at `sentence_start`.
columns.body_version_id: Digest of the normalized text every offset in this row indexes into, and part of the identity.  A span means nothing without it, and keying on it is what stops two extractions of one document from colliding on one identity and silently merging.  Append-only per digest, exactly as `document_citations` is.

columns.activity_date: The publisher's timestamp for it, as written (2026-05-11T20:30:49Z), in UTC: an evening step can fall on the next day here while bill_actions.action_date keeps the day the publisher states for the action (119-hr-1703's discharge: 2026-10-01T03:17:50Z here, 2026-09-30 there). Empty where the item states none, as every Bills of Interest - Exchange of Letters item does.

columns.parent_system_code: The parent committee's system code when the activity is a subcommittee's.

columns.display_path: The human-facing path the engine composes, as a Native list. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.element_id: The publisher's own id attribute on the element this node came from.
columns.section_number: The section's own number as displayed (Sec. 1), where it has one.
columns.heading: The section's header text, empty where the node carries none.

columns.version_date: The parent printing's date, carried so this table versions with its parent.
columns.congress: The Congress of the bill, the prefix of bill_id (119 for 119-hr-1), so a host can store the table one file per Congress.
columns.body_version_id: Stable identity of the substantive captured document body, independent of extraction processing.

columns.policy_area: Publisher policy-area name after trimming, or NULL when the returned answer has no policy area.

columns.bill_id: The bill this summary describes.
columns.version_code: The printing this summary was written from.
columns.printing_id: Which acquisition path supplied that printing.
columns.summary: The plain-language paragraph, length-checked before it was stored.
columns.audience: The short phrase naming the most-affected audience.
columns.top_provisions: Up to three notable provisions, as a Native list in the model's order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.money_bill_kind: The money-bill kind that selected the framing sentence.

columns.bill_id: The bill this printing belongs to.
columns.version_code: The printing's code: its stage's sealed slug, or a numbered reprint's own package suffix (eas2).
columns.printing_id: Which acquisition path supplied this row (govinfo, congress, govinfo-pdf, upload).
columns.label: The publisher's version-type string verbatim, which is not unique per printing.
columns.version_date: Congress textVersions action-associated date for this printing, not its online publication time; the merge prefers the larger value. NULL when absent or when the publisher states an empty `<date/>` (as on enrolled printings, whose dc:date is also empty): order printings with printing_order.
columns.package_id: The GovInfo BILLS package id, read from a stated format URL rather than derived by name.
columns.version_code_is_reprint_ambiguous: True when the publisher's version-type string also names a numbered reprint, so the slug alone cannot tell the two printings apart.
columns.publisher_stage: The root's own bill-stage or resolution-stage attribute: the publisher's word for it.
columns.section_count: How many content-bearing nodes the flattening produced; the bill_sections row count.
columns.equivalent_xml_version_code: For a PDF twin, the version_code of the XML row it stands in for.

columns.kind: Interpreted document kind: `full_text`, `kind_uncertain` (a full-text slug whose measured body yielded zero sections or zero bytes), `procedural_amendments`, `procedural_summary`, or `unknown`.
columns.kind_label: The display label for this kind, supplied by the caller that owns the vocabulary.
columns.kind_warning: The inline warning this kind carries, for a version picker.  NULL for `full_text` and for `unknown`, which states none of its own.
columns.publication_dates: Native SUMMARY and MODS date observations, preserving values, precision, attributes and exact evidence locators. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.publication_evidence_status: Whether SUMMARY was bracketed or changed; every status leaves the metadata/body version link unverified.
columns.body_version_id: Stable identity of the substantive captured document body, independent of extraction processing.

columns.bill_id: The bill whose action carried this entry, keyed as every bill table keys it.
columns.chamber: The chamber that took the roll call, lowercased (house, senate).
columns.congress: The numbered Congress the roll call belongs to.
columns.session: The session number within that Congress, from the entry's sessionNumber.
columns.roll_number: The roll-call number within that session, from the entry's rollNumber.
columns.action_index: Position of the action this entry sat on, in the publisher's own newest-first action order at the capture; it rises as actions are added, so it is not a stable key across captures.
columns.date: The instant the entry states for the vote.
columns.full_action_name: The guide's seventh field, absent on every entry measured; NULL where the publisher sends none.

columns.package_id: The GovInfo package id; package_id and last_modified identify this retained revision.
columns.fiscal_year: The fiscal year this volume is the budget for, as the MODS states it in `field name="Fiscal Year"`, falling back to the year the package id itself carries where the MODS states none.  Not the year it was issued: BUDGET-2026-MSR was issued 2025-09-05.
columns.part: Which part of the budget this volume is, in the publisher's own id spelling (`APP` for the Appendix, `MSR` for the Mid-Session Review).  The sealed vocabulary is in `sources/govinfo/bodies.py`'s package-id grammar, so a part no measurement has seen is a refusal rather than a row.
columns.title: The volume's title as the keyed summary states it.
columns.date_issued: The date the package was issued, as the summary states it.
columns.last_modified: The publisher's package addition/update timestamp, including metadata-only updates. Together with package_id it identifies a retained revision; it is not first publication or a promise that every text change has a unique timestamp.
columns.stated_page_count: How many pages the volume has, as the keyed summary's own `pages` field states it -- never re-derived from the bytes, so a capped read reports how far it got beside the document's own extent rather than publishing its own count as the volume's.
columns.associated_bill_count: How many bills the MODS names; every one is in associated_bills.
columns.associated_bills: Every root-level `<bill>` the MODS names, as a Native list of objects carrying the bill's natural key and the publisher's own `context` marker, in document order.  Published whole because it is the only statement of this edge that carries a Congress: a budget volume's print names a bill without one, so a printed key can be compared with these only congress-blind and can join `congress_bills` not at all. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.associated_law_count: How many laws the MODS names; every one is in associated_laws.
columns.associated_laws: Every root-level `<law>` the MODS names, as a Native list of joined `laws` identities, in document order.  This is what distinct_laws_beyond_index is measured against. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.associated_usc_section_count: How many U.S. Code sections the MODS names; every one is in associated_usc_sections.
columns.associated_usc_sections: Every `<USCode>` *section* the MODS names, as a Native list of objects carrying the `{title}-{section}` key and the publisher's own subsection detail, in document order.  A chapter-only or appendix-only block contributes nothing: neither is a section and neither has a hosted key. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.associated_cfr_part_count: How many CFR parts the MODS names; every one is in associated_cfr_parts.
columns.associated_cfr_parts: Every `<cfr>` part the MODS names, as a Native list of `{title}-{part}` keys, in document order.  Budget volumes are the only sampled collection whose MODS states one at all. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.associated_statute_count: How many Statutes at Large pages the MODS names; every one is in associated_statutes.
columns.associated_statutes: Every `<statuteAtLarge>` page the MODS names, as a Native list of `{volume}-{pages}` keys, in document order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.distinct_bills: How many distinct bills the print names, by the shared citation rules.  A floor bounded by pages_read, and **not a join key**: a budget volume states no Congress, so the rule leaves each one as the congress-free `HR7806` and `congress_bills.bill_id` cannot be built from it.  The MODS's own bill list, which does carry a Congress, is in associated_bills.
columns.distinct_bills_beyond_index_congress_bli: How many of those the MODS does not state **with the Congress dropped from both sides** -- the only comparison this family supports, and the one the re-check made when it reported 6 print-only of 8 distinct across the eight sampled volumes at full page depth.  Named for what it is: a count, never a key, and weaker than every other `*_beyond_index` column here, because two measures numbered alike in different Congresses are one value.  The per-row `document_citations.stated_by_index` stays NULL for bills, because the strict comparison a row would have to claim still cannot be made.
columns.distinct_laws: How many distinct public laws the print names, by the shared citation rules.  A floor, not a total: it counts what pages_read reached.
columns.distinct_laws_beyond_index: How many of those the MODS does not already state.  This is the family's headline: 504 of 518 across the eight sampled volumes at full page depth, against 43 of 69 at the rollup's 60-page cap.  The per-row `document_citations.stated_by_index` carries the same comparison exactly; this column is its summary for one volume.
columns.distinct_usc_sections: How many distinct U.S. Code sections the print names; a floor bounded by pages_read.
columns.distinct_usc_sections_beyond_index: How many of those the MODS does not already state: 97 of 922 across the eight sampled volumes at full page depth.  The MODS states far more than the print here, which is the do-not-recreate rule working in the other direction.
columns.distinct_cfr_parts: How many distinct CFR parts the print names; a floor bounded by pages_read.
columns.distinct_cfr_parts_beyond_index: How many of those the MODS does not already state: 13 of 18 across the eight sampled volumes at full page depth.
columns.distinct_statutes: How many distinct Statutes at Large pages the print names; a floor bounded by pages_read.
columns.distinct_statutes_beyond_index: How many of those the MODS does not already state: 1 of 81 across the eight sampled volumes at full page depth, which is why this kind carries no contract of its own.
columns.citation_rows: How many citation rows this volume produced, across every kind.
columns.body_version_id: Digest of the normalized text the citation spans index into.

columns.bill_id: The bill the source attached this estimate to, as published, keyed the way congress_bills.bill_id is: the bill whose BILLSTATUS record lists it (`billstatus_bulk`), or the bill CBO's feed item names by Bill_Number, by a bare-number Bill_Number and the title's leading citation of that number, or, where Bill_Number is empty, by the citation its title leads with or by the bill the host's laws table says enacted the law it leads with (`cbo_feed`; found_by says which).  Where title_bill_id differs, this number is wrong and title_bill_id names the bill the estimate scores.
columns.congress: The numbered Congress the bill belongs to.
columns.bill_type: Lowercase publisher bill or resolution type (hr, s, hjres...).
columns.bill_number: The measure's number within its Congress and type.
columns.publication_id: CBO's own publication number, parsed from the stated url by the `cbo_publication_url` rule and part of this row's identity.  This is the key CBO's per-Congress feed also states, so that feed's own spelling of the measure, which no GovInfo route gives, joins here.  It is not unique alone: where the routes file one estimate under two bills, both rows publish -- CBO's feed files 22065, its estimate of P.L. 111-322, under the 112th's H.R. 3082 and the 111th's H.R. 3082 BILLSTATUS lists it -- and title_bill_id names the bill it scores.
columns.pub_date: The publisher's pubDate for this estimate; the merge prefers the larger value.  It is when CBO published the estimate, not when the bill acted.  A `cbo_feed` row states the feed's Date as the same instant in UTC, spelled as BILLSTATUS spells pubDate.
columns.title: The estimate's title as the publisher states it, which is usually the bill's own title.
columns.description: CBO's own statement of which printing it scored ("As ordered reported by the House Committee on Energy and Commerce on March 24, 2023").  The only field that distinguishes two estimates of one bill, and the field that states the stage: 826 of the 118th House's 1,062 rows begin "As ordered reported by the House C", and the tail includes Rules Committee prints, which have no committee report at all.  A `cbo_feed` row's is the feed's Description with the surrounding whitespace this package's feed parser trims, a trailing newline on many.
columns.restatements: Every other item naming this publication whose fields differ from the row's, in list order, as a Native list of objects carrying `estimate_index` and only the differing fields; `[]` when they agree or there is no other item.  In the 118th (measured 2026-09-20) 9 of the 37 restated rows differ, every one in `title` alone -- CBO re-spelling the bill's title ('Human rights' to 'Human Rights', one double-escaped ampersand).  In the 108th-111th every row carries its http twin, which differs in `url` and, on all but 11 of 4,762, in `description`, which it wraps in a p element.  The column exists so folding onto the identity drops nothing. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.report_citation_count: How many committee reports this bill's own BILLSTATUS names, on a `cbo_feed` row too, where the host supplies that record; NULL on a `cbo_feed` row shaped without it. Zero means this document names no report citation; it does not establish that no CRPT package exists. 883 of the 1,368 scored bills of the 118th are nonzero (64.5%), and the Senate shortfall is structural -- 155 of 395 scored Senate bills were reported without a written report.
columns.report_citations: Every citation that bill's `<committeeReports>` states, as a Native list in publisher order (NULL where report_citation_count is), each carrying the `citation` verbatim and its parsed `congress`, `report_type` and `number` -- the three columns `committee_reports` publishes -- plus `part` where the citation names one.  A part citation has no package id under GovInfo's sealed CRPT grammar, so none is invented; the parsed parts are NULL on any citation outside the measured shape. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.title_bill_id: The bill this estimate's own title leads with ("H.R. 3447, a bill to extend ..."), keyed as bill_id is and read by the feed's title rule; for a title leading with a public law ("P.L. 111-322, ..."), the bill the host's laws table says enacted it, where the host supplies that map.  NULL where the title leads with no citation, cites the bill only after its start ("Senate Amendment 1183 to S. 744"), is ambiguous, or names a law the host did not map.  Where it differs from bill_id the row is a numbering error and this is the bill the estimate scores: over the 108th-119th (2026-09-28), 5 BILLSTATUS rows and 5 feed rows by bill titles -- four of CBO's own wrong numbers on both, 112 H.R. 1707 for S. 1707 on the feed, and 114 H.R. 3347 on BILLSTATUS, whose record lists CBO's estimate of H.R. 3447 -- and, with a law map, 2 more on both (P.L. 119-21's estimates filed under H. Con. Res. 14) and 1 more on the feed (P.L. 111-322 filed under the 112th's H.R. 3082, its bill's number in the 111th).  A bill citation reads in the row's own Congress, so this cannot show a link to the same number in another Congress: 115 H.R. 1422's BILLSTATUS lists 52538, CBO's estimate of the 113th's H.R. 1422, and this reads 115-hr-1422; that pub_date, 2013-04-22, precedes the 115th.  On a `cbo_feed` row whose found_by is `title`, `title_law` or `bill_number_title` the title chose bill_id, so the two agree by construction and the agreement proves nothing: 237 of the 108th-119th's feed rows with the host's law map, 235 without (2026-09-28).  title_bill_id_rule names the rule.

columns.publication_id: CBO's own publication number, the digits of the item's Link, and this row's identity: no publication is listed twice across the 15,156 items of the 108th-119th feeds (2026-10-03).  cbo_cost_estimates.publication_id joins here, and an item with no row there is one no estimate row holds: one that names no bill (the House's weekly 'Legislation considered under suspension' notices, reconciliation titles, a continuing appropriations act; 53 in the 119th feed on 2026-10-03), a title led by a public law the host's laws table did not map, or a Bill_Number no rule maps, which the family pass refuses by name.
columns.congress: The numbered Congress whose feed lists the item, which a bill it names belongs to.
columns.pub_date: The item's Date as the UTC instant cbo_cost_estimates.pub_date spells it, so the two compare as text; the merge prefers the larger value.  An item whose Date names no instant is a named refusal, not a row (none in the 108th-119th feeds, 2026-10-03).
columns.title: The item's Title as CBO states it, which names the bill where it names one.
columns.link: The item's Link, the publication page on www.cbo.gov, exactly as stated; every measured one is walled.
columns.description: The item's Description as the feed parser trims it, which states the printing scored; NULL where the element is empty, as cbo_cost_estimates.description is.
columns.bill_number: The item's Bill_Number exactly as CBO states it, `` (the empty string) where the element is empty: the feed's own statement that the item names no bill by number.  Every item of the 108th-119th feeds states the element (2026-10-03).  Unparsed here; cbo_cost_estimates.bill_id is the bill a rule reads from it, or from the title where it is empty.

columns.granule_id: GovInfo granule identifier. Primary key / dedup key, including non-section structural units.
columns.part_granule: `'true'` on the granule that is a part itself (an id ending `-part200`, or `-part60-id334` in Title 41), `'false'` on every other row. A part's subparts, subject groups, appendices and table of contents share its `cfr_ref` and read `'false'`, so `part_granule = 'true'` picks the part out of them; a part citation's lookup does exactly that. Read from the granule id alone by SpicyDocs' grammar, never from the heading. A part held in two annual editions has one such row per edition, and a part printed across volumes one per volume (40 CFR part 60 spans volumes 7 to 9 of the 2025 edition).
columns.package_id: GovInfo package identifier for the enclosing annual CFR title and volume.
columns.cfr_ref: Join key to Federal Register `cfr_references`. For a section, the title and its printed citation (e.g. `43-1601.0-1`, `41-50-201.1`); Title 43 keeps its subpart-numbered spelling while `part` names the enclosing part. The Federal Register side cuts every Title 41 compound part at the hyphen (`41 CFR 60-1.4` reads `41-60`), so a Title 41 reference there names a chapter, not a part, and matches no structural row here once the generation carries Title 41's compound parts (see the summary): match it at chapter level (`title = '41' AND part LIKE '60-%'`). NULL for ranges, publisher typos, unprefixed numbers (`Sec. 1-1`), parenthesized citations (`1.401(k)-1`), sections outside a numbered PART and section tokens the volume does not hold; 12 single sections printed with `§§` (`§§ 2.188`) are read as ranges until spicy-docs 0.31.0. For other granules, composed from the part and the identifier's tokens (e.g. `48-700`, `15-746.10-app1`); NULL without a part. A part-level reference (`40-60`) equals `cfr_ref` only on a part's structural rows, of which the part's own granule has `part_granule` `'true'`, and a part held only as sections has none (50 CFR 622 among 12 on 2026-10-03): match a part on `title` and `part`, which section rows carry.
columns.title: CFR title number from the package or granule identifier (e.g. `40`).
columns.part: For a section, the number in the enclosing PART heading of the package's annual volume XML (e.g. `1600`, `50-201`, `241`); NULL outside a numbered PART or when the volume does not hold the section. For a section's appendix or TOC (`sec746-10-app1`), its host section's part when the volume holds the host, else its token's leading number. For other granules, the identifier's part token including letter suffixes (e.g. `1203a`); in Title 41, whose identifiers cut a compound part at the hyphen, the compound part its part granule's heading states (`60-2`).
columns.section: For a section, the printed number less its `{part}.` prefix (e.g. `1` for § 50-201.1, `19-8.1` in Part 241, `1601.0-1` in Part 1600, `401(k)-1`). For a section's appendix or TOC, the rest of its token after the leading number (`10-app1`); for a section token the volume does not hold, the whole token. NULL for other granules.
columns.heading: Granule heading / caption text from GovInfo's list-level `title` field.
columns.edition_year: Annual edition year from the package or granule identifier, falling back to the year in `dateIssued`. This is not necessarily the printed body revision year or proof of a substantive edition.
columns.last_modified: Granule `lastModified` when supplied, otherwise the enclosing package's `lastModified`. GovInfo's granule listing supplies none, so in practice every row carries its package's stamp.

columns.comment_id: The comment's id; its API record is https://api.regulations.gov/v4/comments/{comment_id}.
columns.address1: The submitter's street address, first line, as stated.
columns.address2: The submitter's street address, second line, as stated.
columns.country: The submitter's country, spelled as stated (United States, US, ...).
columns.display_properties: The agency's labels for this record's fields: a Native list of {label, name, tooltip}, name being the attribute it labels; json_column spelling. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.doc_abstract: A summary the agency recorded for the comment; rarely stated.
columns.field1: An agency-defined field; its meaning is the record's display_properties label (“10-Digit HTSUS Item Number for Product of Concern”, “XRIN”, “RTID”, …).
columns.field2: An agency-defined field; its meaning is the record's display_properties label (“File Date”, “Verbal Description for Product of Concern”, …).
columns.file_formats: Renditions of the comment's own content file, rarely stated: a Native list of {fileUrl, format, size}; json_column spelling. Attached files are in the thin table's attachments. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.gov_agency: The government body that submitted the comment.
columns.gov_agency_type: That body's level: Federal, State, Local, Tribal and others.
columns.legacy_id: The comment's id in a predecessor system.
columns.page_count: Pages in the content file, as stated.
columns.postmark_date: The postmark of a comment that arrived by mail, a UTC instant.
columns.reason_withdrawn: The publisher's reason for a withdrawal, spelled as stated.
columns.restrict_reason: Why access is restricted, free text.
columns.restrict_reason_type: The restriction's kind: Copyrighted, Confidential Business Information, Personally Identifiable Information or Other.
columns.state_province_region: The submitter's state, province or region.
columns.submitter_rep: The name of the submitter's representative.
columns.submitter_rep_address: The street address of the submitter's representative, as stated; rarely stated.
columns.submitter_rep_city_state: The city, state and postal code of the submitter's representative, as stated; rarely stated.
columns.withdrawn: Whether the comment has been withdrawn, as the publisher stated it on the record's latest version.

columns.comment_period_id: Stable id of the period (`comment_period_<24 hex>`), from the records that open it.
columns.proceeding_ids: Native list of the proceedings its notices belong to; `[]` when none resolves. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.rins: Native list of the RINs its records state and its proceedings hold. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.docket_ids: Native list of the Regulations.gov dockets anchoring it: those its Register record names, else those of its copies, else a Regulations.gov notice's own; never a feed docket. `[]` where the publishers place the notice in no docket (the Register names none and no copy sits in one, as for FCC-2026-2942-0001), which is not proof that none exists. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.open_date: Eastern day the period opens: the earliest opening among its records (a document's comment start, else its posting; a Register record's publication), `YYYY-MM-DD`.
columns.close_date: Maximum non-placeholder normalized close among grouped records, YYYY-MM-DD: the later of register_close_date and regulations_gov_close_date. Not a legally controlling/current deadline or a submission-purpose classification. Search all three dates; see data_quality.
columns.opened_by_artifact_ids: Native list of public URLs of the records whose window opens the period on `open_date`. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.evidence_ids: Native list of every record in the period, each in exactly one period: dated Register record ids (`number@date`), a notice's Register record included when only its copies state a window, and Regulations.gov document ids. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.anchor_kind: What anchors the period: `docket` when a docket does, `proceeding` when only a proceeding does, `none` when neither; the rulespec export takes the anchored rows.
columns.register_close_date: Latest `comments_close_on` of its Register records, `YYYY-MM-DD`; NULL when the Register states none.
columns.regulations_gov_close_date: Latest comment end (Eastern day) of its Regulations.gov documents, `YYYY-MM-DD`; NULL when none states one.
columns.source: The sources of the dates it takes, `+`-joined: `documents.comment_end_date` and `federal_register.comments_close_on`.
columns.evidence_occurrences: Every accepted source date window before membership lists reduce to sets. Includes source namespace, native document key, source row order, role, dates, and ordered RIN observations. A Register reference requires both document number and publication date; missing older observations remain null. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.unresolved_fr_references_json: JSON array of unresolved Register number references attached to its evidence.

columns.comment_id: Unique comment identifier. Primary key / dedup key.
columns.docket_id: Source-supplied docket identifier for joining to `dockets.docket_id`. Null when the source does not identify a docket; mirror directory names and comment ID prefixes do not fill this field.
columns.comment_on_document_id: Literal Regulations.gov commentOnDocumentId: the named parent document, independently nullable from docket_id. No identifier-prefix inference. The comment re-read filled it: on receipt sha256:77a08369… (2026-10-03) it is set on 26,388,456 of 26,415,400 rows, on at least 98.97% of each of the 12 largest agencies' rows, and below 95% only at MSHA (1,892 of 1,993) and TRAIN (1 of 114). NULL means the record states none or the row was not read; `comment_reference_values_json` tells the two apart. NULL does not mean the comment names no document.
columns.comment_on_object_id: Literal commentOn in the native object-ID namespace; not interchangeable with a public document key.
columns.original_document_id: Publisher `originalDocumentId` when non-blank; NULL when absent, null, or empty/whitespace (verbatim raw value preserved in `comment_reference_values_json`). Retained as an unresolved legacy source reference, not a current key.
columns.comment_reference_values_json: JSON map containing only present source parent-reference fields, preserving null and empty values. {} means the source was read and fields were absent; SQL NULL means legacy or unread.
columns.first_name: Commenter's first name, where the row's read carried it. NULL where the publisher's record states none or where the row's read did not carry the field; `count(first_name)` by `agency_code` is the measure.
columns.last_name: Commenter's last name, where the row's read carried it. NULL where the publisher's record states none or where the row's read did not carry the field; `count(last_name)` by `agency_code` is the measure.
columns.organization: The organization the commenter stated, where the row's read carried it. NULL where the publisher's record states none (FDA and EPA state none; EPA classifies submitters in `subtype` instead) and where the row's read did not carry the field. A campaign record carries it where the publisher states it: on receipt sha256:77a08369… (2026-10-03) FWS states it on 340 of its 408 `Mass Mail Campaign` and 10 of its 13 `Late Mass Mail Campaign` records, EPA on none of 7,842. `count(organization)` by `agency_code` is the measure.
columns.category: Submitter category as regulations.gov states it, where the row's read carried it (FDA's records state one, such as `Individual Consumer` or `Private Industry - C0003`). NULL where the publisher's record states none (EPA states none: it classifies submitters in `subtype` and counts campaigns in `duplicate_comments`) or where the row's read did not carry the field; NULL across a whole agency does not mean the agency does not classify. `count(category)` by `agency_code` is the measure.
columns.title: Comment title / subject line, as the publisher serves it; a few carry HTML entities (`'`, `&`).
columns.comment:
The comment body as regulations.gov serves it: an HTML fragment, not plain text. Line breaks are `
` tags and many characters are HTML entities (`'`, `"`, `&`, `’`) on many rows of every agency, so a pattern with a plain apostrophe or quotation mark misses them: replace the entities before grouping or quoting. Filled for nearly every comment. Text of attached files is in `text_content`, which is filled only where an attachment was extracted. The largest field in the dataset.
columns.document_type: Document category for the comment record, typically `Public Submission`.
columns.posted_date: When the comment was posted, as the publisher stamps it (ISO 8601 string): a date at Eastern midnight written in UTC (`T04:00:00Z` or `T05:00:00Z`) on most records, a bare date label at `T00:00:00Z` on others. Read the date part as the publisher's date; converting a `T00:00:00Z` label to Eastern moves it a day early.
columns.modify_date: Timestamp the comment was last modified (ISO 8601 string).
columns.receive_date: The agency's stated receipt date, stamped as `posted_date` is (ISO 8601 string). It can follow `posted_date` (late or mailed submissions), so compare on the date part.
columns.attachments: Ordered attachments, including restricted entries and renditions without a URL. The attachment's own `attachment_id`, `restrict_reason`, `restrict_reason_type`, `agency_note`, `authors`, `description`, `doc_abstract`, `doc_order`, `modify_date`, and `publication` come from the publisher. Authors are ordered text values and document order is an integer. NULL means the list is absent or unavailable, and [] means the included set had no attachment entries. A NULL field can also mean the comment predates reading that field. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.text_content: Plain text of the comment's attachment(s). Filled inline during the ETL from Mirrulations' own extraction (the bucket's `derived-data` prefix): one extraction tool per comment, its attachments in number order, each stripped and separated by a blank line; when that tool's objects are all blank there is no derived text. Attachments Mirrulations has not extracted are backfilled by the on-demand PDF text-extraction step. Null when neither has produced text; see `text_extraction_status`.
columns.text_extraction_status: Where `text_content` came from, or why there is none. `derived` means Mirrulations' own extraction supplied it (see `pdf_extraction_results_json`); `ok` means Spicy Regs extracted text from at least one PDF, even if another failed; otherwise PDF outcomes prefer `error`, `encrypted`, then `empty`. Derived-data fills written before `derived` existed read `ok` until repaired. Null before an attempt or derived-text fill.
columns.pdf_extraction_results_json: Provenance of `text_content`. For `derived` rows, a JSON object `{comment_id, tool, available_tools, attachments:[{attachment, tool, key, size, etag, sha256}], only_in_other_tools}`: the primary tool (the first of `pypdf`, `pdfminer` with an object for the comment), every tool with an object for it, each attachment's tool, S3 key, listed size and ETag and the SHA-256 of the bytes read (null when the text was kept without re-reading them), and the attachment numbers taken from a tool other than the primary because the primary has no object for them (decision 41); those are in the text. A primary object that exists is kept even when blank. About 125 bytes plus 330 per attachment (31 KB at 92 attachments, the published maximum). Otherwise an ordered JSON array from the latest PDF attempt: `{url, source_sha256, status, page_count, error}` per distinct selected URL; SHA-256 identifies observed bytes, and no-bytes fetch failures have null digest/page count and a generic error. Null when neither is recorded.
columns.subtype: The agency's own class for the submission (regulations.gov `subtype`), spelled as stated. It is agency-specific. EPA classifies the submitter: `Public Comment` (an individual), `Company/Organization Comment`, `Government Local`, `Government State`, `Government Federal`, `Government Tribal`, `Member of Congress`, `Mass Mail Campaign`, `Late Comment`. Most other agencies that state it put one generic label on every record (`Comment(s)`, `Public Comment`, FDA's `Electronic Regulation from Form`), and many state none. EPA's submitter classes also appear at other agencies in small numbers, and `Mass Mail Campaign` (and `Late Mass Mail Campaign`) at several, FWS among them; which agencies state which labels is a query (`SELECT agency_code, subtype, count(*) … GROUP BY ALL`), not a fixed list. Split organizations from individuals only within an agency that classifies, and not by `organization`: all 1,629 records of EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114 leave `organization`, `category` and `first_name` NULL, 219 of them `Company/Organization Comment`. NULL where the record states none or the row predates reading this field.
columns.duplicate_comments: How many received submissions the agency says this posted record stands for (regulations.gov `duplicateComments`), as stated. Agencies that count (EPA and FWS among them) state 1 for a single comment and the campaign's size on a `Mass Mail Campaign` record (15,851 on EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114-1811, National Wildlife Federation Action Fund); agencies that do not count state 0 on every record. Rows are posted records. To estimate submissions, sum `GREATEST(duplicate_comments, 1)`, each posted record standing for at least itself, and first count the NULL rows: GREATEST reads NULL as 1. The sum counts the submissions the agency says its posted records stand for, each record at least itself: its posted accounting, not its official total. On the comments export of receipt sha256:77a08369… (2026-10-03), EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114's 1,629 records sum to 53,692, 52,086 of them on its 23 `Mass Mail Campaign` records, while EPA's response to comments reports about 122,200 received. The 2026-09-28 sample found it stated on every record: 0 on 5,281, 1 on 660, more than 1 on 4. NULL where the row predates reading this field; 0 is a stated zero.
columns.comment_text:
`comment` read as plain text, derived from it each time the mirror is exported and never stored in the catalog. The publisher serves `comment` as an HTML fragment (`I'm`, `
`); this column decodes each character reference once, makes `
` and the end of a block element a newline and a no-break space a space, drops every other tag and trims the ends. Search and quote this column; `comment` keeps the publisher's bytes. The projection loses link targets, list bullets and table layout. One decode only: a body the publisher escaped twice keeps one level (`'` reads `'`), and markup a commenter typed as text (`<br>`) reads as that text. NULL exactly where `comment` is NULL.

columns.agency_code: Agency code of the counted comments.
columns.docket_id: Source docket identifier, or NULL when the source gives none.
columns.year: Year from `posted_date`. NULL when the source posted date is unknown.
columns.month: Month (1–12) from `posted_date`. NULL together with year when the source posted date is unknown.
columns.row_count: Number of posted comment records in the group. These are posted comment records, not comments received: an agency posts one record for a mass-mail campaign that can stand for thousands of submissions (EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114 has 1,629 posted records for about 122,200 comments EPA received). To estimate submissions received, sum `comments.duplicate_comments` as its description says; this table does not carry it.

columns.session: The session the House file states; the Senate file states none.
columns.chamber: Which file the seat came from: house or senate; for a directory row, the member's chamber.

columns.committee_code: The file's own committee code, verbatim; the directory prints none.
columns.is_subcommittee: true for a House subcommittee seat; the Senate file lists full committees only.
columns.parent_system_code: The parent committee's systemCode for a subcommittee seat.
columns.committee_name: The committee's name as the file or directory itself states it.
columns.bioguide_id: The member's bioguide id, which both files state; the key's target is members.bioguide_id.
columns.lis_id: The Senate file's own LIS id for the senator; the crosswalk table stays the LIS crosswalk.
columns.name_last: The member's last name as the file spells it. A directory row's is the member record's, the surname matched as written ("Van Hollen"); the printed form stays in printed_entry.
columns.name_first: The member's first name as the file spells it.
columns.party: The member's party as the file states it.
columns.state: The member's state code as the file states it. A directory row's is the member's own (the term in force or the edition's member record); a misprinted state stays in printed_entry.
columns.district: The House member's district as the file states it.
columns.rank: The House file's rank on the committee; the Senate file states none. A directory row's rank is its print order within its column, the chair first on the majority side; null for another line printed above the columns (a vice chair).
columns.position: The seat's stated role, verbatim: the House leadership attribute or the Senate position attribute. A directory row's role is normalized (Chairman becomes Chair); see position_basis.
columns.source_granule: The GovInfo directory granule the seat is printed in, which names its edition; for a manual reading, the edition's package; for an archived chamber file, its archive URL.
columns.source_line: The 1-based line of the granule's text where the seat's entry starts; for a manual reading, PDF page:line of its layout text.
columns.edition_date: For a directory row, the edition's dateIssued: the date the printed roster describes.
columns.position_basis: For a directory row with a position: `printed`, or `inferred` for a Ranking Member taken from print position (the first minority-column entry) where none is printed.
columns.printed_entry: For a directory row, the entry as printed (name and state), kept when a value was corrected.
columns.entry_label: For a directory row: `corrected` when a printed value was corrected (printed_entry keeps it), `after_departure` when the edition prints a member who had left, `no_congress_gov_code` when the printed body has no Congress.gov code (system_code is then directory-defined).

columns.congress: The Congress of the edition that prints the entry.
columns.congress_basis: `directory`, or `directory-manual` for a reviewed one-off reading of an edition's PDF.
columns.source_granule: The GovInfo directory granule (or, for a manual reading, package) that prints it.
columns.source_line: The 1-based granule line (or, for a manual reading, PDF page:line) where the entry starts.
columns.side: The printed column: chair, majority, minority, single, or line for text read as a whole line.
columns.kind: `vacancy`, `not_a_committee` (a party organization such as the NRCC), `unread_text` (printed text the reader could not seat), `unresolved_seat` (a seat whose committee or member could not be resolved) or `duplicate_seat` (a second printing of a seat already published).
columns.committee_name: The committee or organization title the entry is printed under.
columns.subcommittee_name: The subcommittee title, where the entry is printed under one.

columns.chamber: The publisher's chamber value, lowercased as its address spells it (house, senate, joint, nochamber). NoChamber stays nochamber, not an inferred chamber.
columns.event_id: The publisher's event id, the key hearing_transcripts.event_id joins on.
columns.title: The meeting title as the detail states it.
columns.meeting_date: The meeting's date-time instant as the detail states it.
columns.committee_system_code: System code of the first committee the detail lists.
columns.committee_count: How many committees the detail lists; every one is in committees, and NULL where it is NULL.
columns.committees: Every committee the detail lists, as a Native list of the publisher's objects. NULL where no detail was read or the detail states no such list; `[]` where it states an empty one. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.hearing_jacket: The first hearing transcript jacket number the detail lists, where it lists any.
columns.hearing_jacket_count: How many transcript jackets the detail lists; every one is in hearing_jackets, and NULL where it is NULL.
columns.hearing_jackets: Every transcript jacket number the detail lists, as a Native list of strings. NULL where no detail was read or the detail states no such list; `[]` where it states an empty one. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.bill_count: How many bills the detail relates to the meeting; every one is in bill_ids, and NULL where it is NULL.
columns.bill_ids: Natural keys of every bill in relatedItems.bills, as a Native list, in publisher order; a bill named only in a meeting document is not here. NULL where no detail was read or the detail states no relatedItems.bills; `[]` where it states an empty one. This is the gate and a heading is never one: three retained reports print a CBO heading over a section saying the estimate was not received, and one prints the estimate under a heading no pattern set had.  `false` is requested-empty with estimate_absence_reason attached, never absence: 3 of 13 reported bills whose index named an estimate had none in the report.

columns.part_number: The part's number as the publisher states it (its `partNumber`, or the `-pt{N}` its id carries, which must agree). columns.law_type: The publisher's law type for the first laws entry (Public Law or Private Law).
columns.statutes_at_large_cite: NULL here on purpose: the citation is published on laws.statutes_at_large_cite, read from the PLAW USLM meta, and the host fills this column by joining laws on bill_id at merge time. The family build sees one BILLSTATUS document and its printings; the PLAW is a different package the laws rollup acquires once per law, so filling it here would fetch every PLAW twice or read another table's output, which the one-pass rule forbids.
columns.stage: The whole bill's interpreted legislative stage: the latest step its actions show under the current rule, not a final outcome. On the ladder: `introduced`, `committee`, `calendared`, `passed_chamber`, `other_chamber`, `passed_both`, `conference`, `cleared`, `presented` or `law` (the terminal rung; the literal is `law`, never `enacted`); or an outcome with no rung, `failed` or `vetoed`. `introduced` is also the default when no rule fires (see stage_rule); NULL where the bill's actions were not examined, which is not a statement about enactment. A number the House reserves for its leadership (title "Reserved for the Speaker.") has no actions: it reads `introduced` with stage_rule NULL, or NULL where GovInfo holds no document. A mention is not an event: taking over the sponsorship of a bill "originally introduced by" another, a floor action citing the text "as introduced" or "as reported", a special rule's report or description, and a star print classify nothing, and where the publisher's action code names a step, the code is read before the text. `calendared` is a placement on the Union, House or Senate Legislative Calendar in the bill's own chamber (a reported bill awaiting the floor, or one placed there unreported under Senate Rule XIV or a discharge); a later report, order to report, subcommittee referral or floor step leaves it `calendared`, and only a referral of the bill to a committee lowers it. `passed_chamber` and `other_chamber` both mean the bill's own chamber has passed it; `other_chamber` adds that the other chamber has received it or taken a calendar, desk or floor step on it. A calendar placement, the desk, a motion to proceed or cloture reads `other_chamber` only where the chamber that took it (as the text names it, else the system that entered it) is not the one the bill's type originates in; in its own chamber the desk, a motion to proceed or cloture moves nothing. `passed_both` means both chambers have passed it (the Library of Congress's 8000 and 17000 where the actions carry codes, else the text) but not, as far as the wording shows, in one text: the second passage carried an amendment the other chamber has not agreed to, or names none either way (the House's "On passage Passed"), and the publisher lists no enrolled text. It is read from the passage that completed it. `conference` is a conference requested, held or reported; the Library of Congress's "Resolving differences" exchange of amendments is not one. `cleared` means both chambers have agreed to one text: the second chamber passed it as it arrived (the Senate "without amendment", or the House on a motion to suspend the rules that names no amendment), a chamber agreed to the other's amendment with no amendment of its own, or both agreed to a conference report; the Library of Congress's "Cleared for White House." (109th-111th Congresses) reads it too. So does a measure both chambers passed in wording that states no agreement (the House's "On agreeing to the resolution Agreed to" on a Senate concurrent resolution) where its BILLSTATUS document lists an enrolled text, GPO's final copy of a measure both chambers passed in identical form. A bill or joint resolution is then ready for the President; a concurrent resolution is complete. `failed` is the latest vote on passage failing in either chamber, a failed two-thirds vote to suspend the rules included: the measure can still pass, and it reads over an earlier passage by the other chamber until a later step. `vetoed` stands until a recorded enactment; a failed override keeps it. The stage never moves back once a chamber has passed the bill: the other chamber's referral or report, a star print or an introduction phrase does not lower it, and only a passage the Senate states it vitiated is undone; where the actions carry publisher codes, the Library of Congress's passage code (8000 House, 17000 Senate) is what holds it. Once `cleared`, no lower rung moves it back. A motion's or a point of order's result ("motion to proceed ... agreed to in Senate") is not the measure's passage, and "disagreed to in Senate" reads `failed`.
columns.stage_rule: Which rule fired: a stage's own name where that rule read the action's text (`introduced`, `committee`, `calendared`, `passed_chamber`, `other_chamber`, `conference`, `cleared`, `presented`, `law`), `cleared` also for both chambers' agreement to a conference report, read from the second; `vetoed` for the President's veto; `failed_passage` for a failed vote on passage, a failed veto override included (which leaves the stage `vetoed`); `action_code` where the Library of Congress's passage or presentation code decided it; `became_law_code` for the publisher's became-law code; `passed_both` for the passage that left both chambers' passages standing; `enrolled_text_listed` for `cleared` read from the enrolled text the BILLSTATUS document lists, not from an action. NULL when no rule fired and the default stood.
columns.stage_source_text: The full action text the stage rule matched against, never shortened; for enrolled_text_listed, the listed text version's type as the publisher states it ("Enrolled Bill").
columns.signed_date: The date of the publisher's coded became-law action (36000, E40000 or the BecameLaw type) for a public or a private law; NULL where the bill states no law, or states one with no coded action.
columns.signed_date_rule: Which signed-date rule produced that answer: `public_law_and_became_law_action`, `private_law_and_became_law_action`, `public_law_without_became_law_action` (a public law with no coded action, so no date) or `no_public_law` (no law entry, or a private law with no coded action).
columns.money_bill_kind: Interpreted money-bill kind, or NULL when no rule claimed the measure. A title heuristic with unmeasured recall: an appropriations act whose title lacks the pattern, or an appropriations division inside another bill, is NULL (money_bill_rule names the rule that fired). A simple or concurrent resolution (H. Res., S. Res., H. Con. Res., S. Con. Res.) is never a money bill, though a House special rule names the one it brings up, and `omnibus` is an appropriations omnibus only, not a statute named "Omnibus" (the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act).
columns.fiscal_year: Fiscal year the display title states, spelled FY plus the year: `fiscal year 2027`, the long title's `for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027`, or an appropriations act's closing year (`... Appropriations Act, 2027`, `Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027`). Never read from short_title, which a reused vehicle takes from the act it replaced. NULL where the title states none.

Read only where the regular-appropriations rule (or a manual override) classified the bill.

Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

columns.published_date: The publisher's `publishDate` for this retained report version, as the list route states it. Dates the version, not necessarily the first issue (R44997, first issued in 2017, carries 2026-04-29 at version 16). The list route gives no first-issue date.

columns.display_properties: The agency's labels for this record's fields: a Native list of {label, name, tooltip}, name being the attribute it labels; json_column spelling. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.effective_date: When the action takes effect, a UTC instant.
columns.exhibit_location: Where a physical exhibit is held.
columns.field1: An agency-defined field; its meaning is the record's display_properties label (“Answer Date”, “XRIN”, “RTID”, …).
columns.field2: An agency-defined field; its meaning is the record's display_properties label (labelled “File Date”).

columns.state_province_region: The submitter's state, province or region.
columns.subject: The subject line.
columns.submitter_rep: The name of the submitter's representative.
columns.subtype: The agency's subtype: Correspondence, Report, Decision and others.
columns.topics: The publisher's topics, in its order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.within_comment_period: Whether the document arrived within the comment period, where given, as the publisher stated it on the record's latest version; the comment window's state comes from its dates.

columns.document_key: The citing document's own natural key in its family's spelling: the GovInfo `packageId` for a package, and one value per family as the table takes each one.
columns.document_kind: Which family the citing document belongs to, so one table serves all of them.
columns.cite_kind: What kind of thing is cited, by the rule that read it: `bill_number`, `public_law`, `statutes_at_large`, `usc_section`, `cfr_section`, `federal_register_cite`, `rin`, `gao_product_id`, `crs_report_id`, `docket_number`, `case_docket_number`, `us_reports_cite` or `committee_name`.
columns.target_key: The cited key in the hosted target's own spelling, which is part of this row's identity: `congress_bills.bill_id` for a bill, the joined `laws` identity for a law, a committee's `system_code`.  Where nothing settled it, the rule's canonical form of the printed text stands instead and `target_resolved` says so, because an unsettled key is still evidence and dropping it would lose what only the print holds.
columns.span_start: Character offset of the match in the document's normalized text, counted from zero.  Part of the identity: one document naming one bill forty times is forty rows, and the offset is what tells them apart.
columns.span_end: Character offset just past the match, so `text[span_start:span_end]` is `matched_text`.
columns.matched_text: The exact characters the rule matched, so a false positive is readable from the row without the document in hand.
columns.target_resolved: Whether `target_key` is the hosted target's own spelling.  `false` means the rule found the cite but nothing settled the key: a bill with no stated Congress, or a committee name no supplied roster reaches.  A shape check, not an existence check: a resolved key can name nothing the target table holds; join the target table to learn whether it is held.
columns.target_rule: How the key was reached. Bill routes distinguish inline_congress, congress_subheading, document_fallback, unstated and document_fallback_refused after the bill_number: prefix. A document fallback is context supplied by the caller, not proof of historical applicability. Other kinds use the rule name except `committee_name`, where it is the resolution route: `exact` and `roster_prefix` are lookups in the roster vocabulary, while `name_prefix` and `sibling_prefix` are inferences from the printed text of this one document.  A consumer wanting only roster lookups filters on this column rather than on `target_resolved`.
columns.stated_by_index: Whether a keyed index record for this document already states this target key -- the package MODS's own `<bill>`, `<law>` and `<USCode>` section elements and its authoring committee.  NULL where no index record was supplied.  This is the owner's do-not-recreate rule, carried per row: where it is `true` the row's value is the evidence span, not the key, and `WHERE stated_by_index IS NOT TRUE` selects the kinds that are genuinely new.
columns.body_version_id: Digest of the normalized text the offsets index into, and part of the identity.  A span means nothing without it -- a re-extraction that moved one character moves every offset after it -- and keying on it is what stops two extractions of the same document from colliding on one identity and silently merging.  The table is append-only per digest: a superseded extraction's rows are not retired, and a consumer filters to the digest `house_activity_reports.text_sha256` states for that document.
columns.target_table: The namespace the target key belongs to, as the rule names it (`congress_bills`, `gao products (product id as GAO prints it)`): what the key identifies, not whether a host holds a table of it.

columns.document_id: Unique document identifier. Primary key / dedup key.
columns.docket_id: Parent docket this document belongs to. Foreign key to `dockets.docket_id`.
columns.agency_code: Posting agency's short code. `lookup_agency` resolves it through RefSpec's REF-038 projection: measured 2026-10-30, 307 of 316 codes on 2,003,671 of 2,004,396 rows; the rest (`USC`, `BSC`, `TRAIN`, `PCSCOTUS`, `GAPFAC`, `ERULE`, `ARCTICGAS`, `PRES`, `EOA`) have no projection row.
columns.title: Document title.
columns.document_type: Coarse document category (e.g. `Rule`, `Proposed Rule`, `Notice`, `Supporting & Related Material`). For finer agency subtypes such as Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM), Extension of Comment Period, Interim Final Rule, or Withdrawal, join `document_attributes` 1:1 on `document_id` and read `document_attributes.subtype`.
columns.posted_date: Date the document was posted publicly (ISO 8601 string).
columns.modify_date: Timestamp the document was last modified (ISO 8601 string).
columns.comment_start_date: Literal Regulations.gov commentStartDate. See data_quality for the source-specific calendar conversion; this field does not establish submission purpose. NULL means no value was retained.
columns.comment_end_date: Literal Regulations.gov commentEndDate as Regulations.gov states it now, which can reflect a later extension rather than the notice's own date: when a later notice extends the period, Regulations.gov can rewrite the original notice's date too (FS-2025-0001-223869, FR 2026-16965, reads 2026-10-07T03:59:59Z, the extension FR 2026-18648 set, while the Register's comments_close_on for 2026-16965 is 2026-09-21). For the date a notice printed, read federal_register.comments_close_on by fr_doc_num. Convert offset-bearing instants to America/New_York for calendar searches; date-only values and the source's bare T00:00:00Z convention keep their printed day (see data_quality). Neither purpose nor the controlling/current deadline follows from this field; inspect filing instructions and later notices. NULL does not mean no deadline.
columns.attachments: Native list of the main document's fileFormats renditions: `[{url, format, size}]`. This compatibility field does not contain separately listed attachment resources. Null when no main renditions were retained. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.attachment_records: Native list of the main document's fileFormats renditions: `[{url, format, size}]`. This compatibility field does not contain separately listed attachment resources. Null when no main renditions were retained. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.fr_doc_num: Federal Register document number, when the document was published in the FR. Often null.
columns.withdrawn: Whether regulations.gov flags the posting withdrawn, as the string `"true"`/`"false"`. Often null. A withdrawn posting is still held here; the rulemaking tables read it as no evidence (see `proceedings`).
columns.reason_withdrawn: Agency-supplied reason for withdrawal, when withdrawn: usually that it was posted to the wrong docket, a duplicate, moved or replaced. Often null.
columns.additional_rins: Native list of additional Regulation Identifier Numbers beyond the docket's primary RIN. Rarely populated on regulations.gov, so not a usable RIN join key; use `federal_register.regulation_id_numbers` or `fr_docket_links.regulation_id_numbers_json` instead. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.text_content: Plain text extracted from the document's PDF attachment(s) by the PDF text-extraction step. Null until that step has run; see `text_extraction_status`.
columns.publisher_status: What Regulations.gov last said of the document when the daily reconcile step checked its docket: `listed` (the docket's document listing names it, or, where the listing does not, its own record still answers) or `removed` (the listing omits it and its own record answers 404 or 410). NULL where the step has never checked it: it checks only dockets with a document posted or modified in the past week, so NULL does not mean the publisher still serves it. A removed document stays in this table (see data_quality).
columns.removed_observed_at: When the reconcile step first found the document removed, as a UTC ISO 8601 instant; NULL unless `publisher_status` is `removed`.
columns.file_url: URL of the document's primary downloadable rendition. Retained for backward compatibility; see `attachments` for the full list. Often null.
columns.text_extraction_status: Aggregate PDF outcome: `ok` means at least one PDF supplied text, even if another failed; otherwise `error`, `encrypted`, or `empty` (no extractable text) in that order. Null before an attempt. See `pdf_extraction_results_json` for each file.
columns.pdf_extraction_results_json: Ordered JSON array from the latest PDF attempt: `{url, source_sha256, status, page_count, error}` per distinct selected URL. SHA-256 identifies observed bytes; no-bytes fetch failures have null digest/page count and a generic error. Null when no PDF attempt is recorded. Describes that attempt, not the provenance of older text retained after a failed overwrite.

columns.id_submission: ECFS submission id (e.g. `26109947027`). Primary key / dedup key. The filing's page on fcc.gov is `https://www.fcc.gov/ecfs/filing/<id_submission>`: the former `filing_url` column, which this table does not hold.
columns.proceedings: Source-listed FCC proceedings with their names and identifiers; repeated occurrences remain distinct. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.submission_type: ECFS submission type description, e.g. `COMMENT`, `REPLY TO COMMENTS`, `NOTICE OF EXPARTE`.
columns.express_comment: Publisher express-comment flag, normalized to BOOLEAN. NULL means the publisher omitted the flag or supplied null; retained native evidence distinguishes those states. The flag alone does not establish document availability.
columns.date_received: Timestamp ECFS records the filing as received (ISO 8601 string). Incremental cursor and sort key.
columns.date_submission: Timestamp the filer submitted the filing (ISO 8601 string).
columns.date_disseminated: Timestamp the filing was disseminated (made public) by ECFS (ISO 8601 string).
columns.exparte_or_late_filed: `Y` if the filing is ex-parte or late-filed, else `N`.
columns.filers: Native list of filer names (individuals or organizations) on the filing. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.authors: Native list of author names on the filing, when distinct from the filers. Often empty. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.lawfirms: Native list of law-firm names on the filing. Often empty. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.bureaus: Native list of FCC bureau names the filing was routed to. Often empty. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.text_data: The filing's inline text — for express comments this is the full comment text. Null for document-only filings.
columns.total_page_count: Total page count across the filing's attached documents, as a numeric string.
columns.documents: Native list of attached documents as `{filename, src}` objects, where `src` is the fcc.gov download URL. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.generation_id: Selected main filing generation. Binds retained result observations to this filing version; it is not the original attempt time.
columns.extraction_results: Latest retained extraction results in source order: URL, status, body digest, page count, error and matching offered document positions. Null means no result was recorded; an empty list means the retained result list was empty. Repeated offers keep every position. Capture custody and extracted-text access remain unverified. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

columns.name: Proceeding (docket) number, e.g. `17-108` or `23-320`. Primary key / dedup key, and the join key to the `name` of each entry in `fcc_filings.proceedings`.
columns.id_proceeding: ECFS numeric identifier, reused across some docket names in retained data (301759 appears with both 17-108 and 87-432). Native filing-to-proceeding joins require name AND id_proceeding; the numeric ID alone is not globally unique. The table's primary key remains name.
columns.description: Proceeding title/subject (ECFS `description_display`, falling back to `description`), e.g. `Restoring Internet Freedom`. There is no program or topic field, and titles often leave the program out: Universal Service dockets include 13-184 (`Modernizing the E-rate Program for Schools and Libraries.`) and 02-60 (`In the Matter of Rural Health Care Support Mechanism`), neither of which says universal service, and high-cost programs such as the Rural Digital Opportunity Fund (19-126) and the 5G Fund (20-32) use their own names. Search titles together with bureau_code (WC, or CC for older dockets) and known docket numbers, and find related dockets by the proceedings filings name alongside an anchor docket in `fcc_filings.proceedings` (for Universal Service, the umbrella docket 96-45 and 10-90). A title search gives a floor, not a complete list.
columns.bureau_code: Code of the FCC bureau that owns the proceeding (e.g. `WC`).
columns.bureau_name: Name of the FCC bureau that owns the proceeding (e.g. `Wireline Competition Bureau`).
columns.rulemaking_or_docket: ECFS `flag_rulemaking_or_docket`: `R` for rulemakings (RM- numbers), `D` for dockets.
columns.filing_status: ECFS filing-window status for the proceeding (e.g. `OPENALL`): how filings are accepted, not whether the proceeding is open. Many closed proceedings still read `OPENALL`; see date_closed for the record-level closure convention.
columns.date_created: Timestamp the proceeding was created in ECFS (ISO 8601 string). Sort key.
columns.date_closed: ECFS-recorded closure timestamp. NULL or a future date can be used only as a record-level open convention; placeholders include 2099-12-31T23:59:59.999Z and 2100-01-31T05:00:00.000Z. Neither this convention nor a recorded closure establishes current legal effect, filing acceptance or an active comment period. Check filing_status and the specific notice's comment/reply instructions separately.
columns.filed_by: ECFS account that created the proceeding. An internal FCC username; occasionally useful for spotting bureau conventions.
columns.date_nprm: ECFS `date_nprm`: date of the proceeding's Notice of Proposed Rulemaking as ECFS records it, an ISO 8601 string with the publisher's UTC offset as written (96-82: `1996-04-01T00:00:00.000-05:00`). NULL when ECFS records none; 6,023 of 21,705 dockets carry one (retained walk 2026-10-08).
columns.date_reporting_and_order: ECFS `date_reporting_and_order`: date of the Report and Order as ECFS records it, an ISO 8601 string with the publisher's UTC offset as written (96-82: `1996-10-18T00:00:00.000-04:00`). NULL when ECFS records none; 5,290 of 21,705 dockets carry one (retained walk 2026-10-08).
columns.rule_section: ECFS `rule_section`: the CFR part or section the proceeding concerns, as typed by FCC staff (96-82: `PART 80 AND 87`; 96-96: `73.202(B)`). Free text, not a normalized citation. Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped and a blank value is NULL (owner decision 2026-10-31): ECFS writes an empty string or a single space where it has none and pads some values (` Part 76`); the ECFS pages each run retains keep the value as ECFS wrote it. 11,259 of 21,705 dockets carry text, 16 of them stripped (retained walk 2026-10-08).

Committees often file a placeholder instead (`NONE`, `N/A`, `-`, and until 2016 `BLANK`), kept verbatim as FEC's own committee master carries it: read one as no connected organization (schemas.fec_committee_history.is_placeholder_name says which values are).
columns.candidate_id: The candidate the committee is linked to that cycle (`CAND_ID`); NULL when none.

columns.committee_id: OpenFEC committee identifier (e.g. `C00684373`). Primary key / dedup key. Joins `fec_committee_history.committee_id` for per-cycle names and the connected organization.
columns.name: Committee name as registered with the FEC.
columns.committee_type: Single-letter committee type code (e.g. `P` presidential, `H` House, `S` Senate, `N`/`Q`/`O` PAC variants).
columns.designation: Single-letter committee designation code (e.g. `P` principal campaign committee, `A` authorized, `U` unauthorized, `J` joint fundraiser).
columns.party: Political party code, when set (e.g. `DEM`, `REP`, `W`). Often null for non-party committees.
columns.party_full: Human-readable political party (e.g. `DEMOCRATIC PARTY`, `WRITE-IN`). Often null.
columns.state: Two-letter state associated with the committee. Often null.
columns.organization_type_full: Human-readable sponsoring organization type (e.g. `Corporation`, `Labor Organization`, `Trade Association`). Often null.
