columns.term_match: `half_open` (one term with start <= day < end), `inclusive_end` (none half-open, exactly one with the end day included), `ambiguous` (more than one term either way), `unmatched` (none), `unresolved_member`, or `undated` (the file prints no date, so no term is chosen). `undated` wins over `unresolved_member`; such a row still carries `bioguide_id` wherever the member resolves.
columns.term_index: The matched term's `term_index` in `member_terms`; NULL unless matched.
columns.term_start: The matched term's start date; NULL unless matched.
columns.term_end: The matched term's end date; NULL unless matched.

columns.vote_id: The roll call this position belongs to, as roll_call_votes keys it.
columns.congress: The numbered Congress the roll call belongs to.
columns.session: The session number within that Congress.
columns.roll_number: The roll-call number within that session.
columns.member_key: The file-stated id: `lis:` plus the LIS id on a Senate record, the bare bioguide id on a House one, and `name:` plus the publisher's name where the file states neither (every Clerk file of 1990-2002). A Senate bioguide comes from the crosswalk and does not always resolve, so keying on it would split one member's votes across two rows; an identity column also cannot be null, which the design's bioguide key would have been. A `name:` key identifies the row within its roll call, not a person: across 1990-2002 at least 21 of the Clerk's labels name two different members (Jones (NC), Allen, Schiff, Wilson, McHugh, Smith (WA)...), so a person is the host's crosswalk, never this key. Congress, member_name, party and state do not identify one either: one Congress can seat a successor of the same surname, party and state (where the Clerk states bioguide ids, 5 such keys name two: 109th Matsui D-CA, 110th Carson D-IN, 112th Payne D-NJ, 117th Letlow R-LA, 119th Grijalva D-AZ; in 1990-2002 the 105th's Capps and Bono (CA) and the 107th's Shuster (PA) show it as a gap inside the Congress), so the crosswalk adds vote_date, checked against each member's service dates.
columns.bioguide_id: The voting member's bioguide id: stated by the publisher on a House row (the Clerk's name-id, from 2003), and filled by the host's crosswalk at merge time on a Senate row, whose file states only lis_id (members.lis_id resolves it); NULL where neither supplies one.
columns.lis_id: The voting member's Senate LIS id, which only the Senate file carries.
columns.member_name: The member's name exactly as the roll-call source spells it.
columns.party: The member's party as the roll-call source states it.
columns.state: The member's state as the roll-call source states it. On a House row `XX` is the Clerk's marking for the non-voting delegates and the Resident Commissioner, on the roll calls they voted in: 2,169 of the Clerk's 22,512 of 1990-2026 (1993-1994, 2007-2010, 2019-2020 and from 2022; none in 2021), every one an amendment vote or a motion in committee (to rise, to strike or limit debate, a call in committee, a ruling of the chair), filed under <committee> (clerk_body_element on roll_call_votes) from 2007 and under <chamber> in 1993-1994.  Kept as stated, not mapped to a territory.
columns.position: The member's position exactly as the publisher spelled it (Yea, Aye, Not Voting...).
columns.position_normalized: That position folded onto yea, nay, present or not_voting; NULL for a named candidate choice.
columns.vote_date: The chamber's literal date; sorts as text, not by time (see roll_call_votes `vote_day`).

columns.bioguide_id: The Biographical Directory id, which is this crosswalk's primary identifier.
columns.bioguide_previous: The source list of previous Bioguide ids in its order, as JSON; absent is NULL. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.lis_id: The Senate LIS id, which only senators carry.
columns.fec_ids: Every FEC candidate id for this person, as a Native list in the publisher's order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.icpsr_id: The ICPSR id used by roll-call research datasets.
columns.votesmart_id: The Vote Smart person id from the community crosswalk; absent when unstated.
columns.name_first: The person's first name as the crosswalk spells it.
columns.name_last: The person's last name as the crosswalk spells it.
columns.other_names: Source other_names patches in order, with literal date bounds and nulls; absent is NULL. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.term_count: How many terms the crosswalk lists; the member_terms row count for this person.
columns.first_term_start: Start date of the earliest term listed.
columns.last_term_end: End date of the latest term listed.
columns.current_term_type: Chamber of the latest term: rep or sen.
columns.current_term_party: Party of the latest term, as the crosswalk states it for that term.
columns.current_term_district: District of the latest term; absent for a Senate term.
columns.name_nickname: The crosswalk's own name.nickname for the person, as it spells it; NULL means the crosswalk states none, not that the person has none.
columns.name_middle: The crosswalk's own name.middle for the person, as it spells it; NULL means the crosswalk states none, not that the person has none.
columns.name_suffix: The crosswalk's own name.suffix for the person, as it spells it; NULL means the crosswalk states none, not that the person has none.
columns.name_official_full: The crosswalk's own name.official_full for the person, as it spells it; NULL means the crosswalk states none, not that the person has none.
columns.roster: Which file this record came from: current or historical.
columns.observed_at: When the file was captured; the merge prefers the larger value.
columns.other_names_json: Source other_names patches in order, with literal date bounds and nulls; absent is NULL.

columns.scope_id: The input's replacement scope, `native_reference_scope_id` over source_family, source_record_key and edition; a complete read replaces every row of its scope, and a successful empty read clears it.
columns.source_family: The scanner family that read the input: `uscode`, `ecfr`, `bill`, `law` or `statute`, fixed by the shaper.
columns.source_record_key: The caller's record identity for the input, retained literally.
columns.edition: The edition or request date the caller's checked capture metadata states, literally; NULL when it states none, never read from a filename.
columns.body_version_id: `sha256:` digest of the exact retained XML bytes the scanner read.
columns.source_locator: Where the caller retained the input from, literally; not proof of acquisition time or edition.
columns.occurrence_index: The observation's zero-based position among the input's observations, both kinds counted together in the order the scanner reported them, as decimal text.
columns.source_path: The observed element's positional XPath in the input (`/*[1]/*[2]`), never a byte offset.
columns.element_tag: The observed element's tag, its namespace expanded (`{http://xml.house.gov/schemas/uslm/1.0}ref`) where the input declares one.
columns.observation_kind: `native_reference` for a bill, law or Statutes at Large observation, `native_reference` or `source_credit` for a U.S. Code observation, `authority` (AUTH) or `source_note` (SOURCE) for an eCFR note.
columns.href: The element's href exactly as stated, an empty string when stated empty; NULL when absent, and on every source credit and note.
columns.text: The complete decoded text of a source credit or note, whitespace kept; NULL on a native reference.
columns.text_runs: An eCFR note's text split at element boundaries, as a Native list whose strings join to text; NULL on U.S. Code rows. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.cfr_title: The CFR title the caller's checked capture metadata states, on an eCFR note; NULL when it states none, never inferred from a fragment.
columns.cfr_part: The `N` of the nearest enclosing DIV5 part on an eCFR note; NULL when no part encloses it, and on U.S. Code rows.
columns.interpretation_status: How the reading under rule_version read this observation: `native_section_href`, `native_statute_href`, `native_public_law_href` or `unsupported_href` for an href, `native_bill_usc_cite` for a qualified bill DTD cite, `partial_text_findings` or `no_qualified_text_findings` for text; it does not claim exhaustive extraction.
columns.target_candidates: The typed targets the reading found, as a Native list in reading order, each with the outcome of the host's lookup in the target tables it selected; several targets in one note stay one row, and an unsupported href has none. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.rule_version: `native-legal-reference/004` (`NATIVE_LEGAL_REFERENCE_RULE`): the scanners' selected shapes and the reading this row was produced under, comparable for equality only.
columns.text_rendition: The named readable-text rendition into which text_span_start and text_span_end index (`uslm-block-boundaries/1`, `ecfr-block-boundaries/1`, or `bill-dtd-block-boundaries/1`); NULL when no text map was produced.
columns.text_offset_unit: The offset unit of text_span_start and text_span_end: `unicode_code_points` (0-based half-open code-point indices in text_rendition); NULL when text_rendition is NULL.
columns.text_rendition_sha256: `sha256:` digest of the UTF-8 encoding of the complete text_rendition string, binding the offsets to the exact rendition beside input_sha256 and source_path; NULL when text_rendition is NULL.
columns.text_span_start: Inclusive 0-based start offset of the observed element's text in text_rendition, as decimal text in text_offset_unit; NULL when the element carries no text or no text map was produced.
columns.text_span_end: Exclusive 0-based end offset of the observed element's text in text_rendition, as decimal text in text_offset_unit, so slicing text_rendition yields span_text; NULL when text_span_start is NULL.
columns.span_text: The exact slice of text_rendition at [text_span_start:text_span_end] for this element; NULL when text_span_start is NULL.
columns.native_element_id: Publisher element identifier attached to this legal reference.
columns.native_idref: Publisher identifier reference attached to this legal reference.
columns.native_class: Publisher classification attached to this legal reference.

columns.nomination_id: Canonical nomination key ({congress}-pn-{number}, plus -{part} when part_number is non-zero).
columns.citation: The publisher's citation, its own display key, with the part where one exists (PN730-20).
columns.congress: The numbered Congress the nomination was received in.
columns.part_number: The part number, as the publisher spells it.
columns.description: The publisher's description of the nomination.
columns.organization: The organization the nominee would serve in.
columns.received_date: The date the Senate received the nomination.
columns.is_civilian: Whether the nomination is civilian, as the publisher's nominationType states it: `true` where it states isCivilian true (or isMilitary false), `false` where it states isMilitary true (or isCivilian false). The list route states exactly one of the two keys (2,287 of 2,287 rows of the 119th, 2026-10-03). NULL where it states neither, or both with contradicting values; nomination_type_json keeps what it stated, so `is_civilian IS NULL AND nomination_type_json IS NOT NULL` counts the contradictions.
columns.is_military: The publisher's nominationType object, as JSON. This column retains the source property isMilitary.
columns.latest_action_date: Date of the publisher's latestAction entry.
columns.latest_action_text: Text of the publisher's latestAction entry.
columns.update_date: The publisher's updateDate; the merge prefers the larger value.
columns.committees_json: Every committee returned by the nomination committees route, in source order; NULL when unread, [] on a complete empty response.
columns.hearings_json: Every printed hearing returned by the nomination hearings route, including jacket number and chamber; NULL when unread, [] on a complete empty response.

columns.organization: Commenter organization exactly as filed on the comment. Join key back to `comments.organization`.
columns.committee_id: Matched OpenFEC committee identifier. Joins to `fec_committees.committee_id`, whose `filing_frequency` (`T` or `A`: terminated) and `last_file_date` say whether the committee still files.
columns.committee_name: Matched committee name as registered with the FEC.
columns.committee_type_full: Human-readable committee type of the matched committee (e.g. `PAC - Qualified`). Never a House, Senate or presidential candidate's committee: those links are left out.
columns.designation_full: Human-readable committee designation of the matched committee. Never `Leadership PAC`: those links are left out.
columns.party_full: Human-readable political party of the matched committee. Often null for non-party committees.
columns.organization_type_full: Sponsoring organization type of the matched committee (e.g. `Trade Association`, `Labor Organization`). Often null.
columns.committee_state: Two-letter state on the matched committee (`fec_committees.state`). Often null.
columns.match_method: How the pair matched: `exact` (full normalized names equal), `core` (decoration-stripped cores equal), or `prefix` (committee core starts with the whole organization core on a token boundary).
columns.confidence: `high` for `exact`/`core`; for `prefix`, `medium` when `committee_match_count` <= 5 and `low` above that. Grades the name match alone: it ignores whether the committee still files and the sponsor FEC states (`sponsor_name_match`). Filter on this to pick a precision bar.
columns.committee_match_count: How many FEC committees this organization name matched in total, counting the candidate committees and leadership PACs whose links are left out, so it can exceed this string's rows here. A high count does not establish an affiliate network; inspect source evidence alongside the matching rule.
columns.comment_count: Comments filed under this exact organization string in every agency and year the comments table holds (deduplicated on `comment_id`, newest `modify_date` wins — matching the MCP `comments` view). The same value repeats on each committee row of the string; do not sum it across rows.
columns.docket_count: Distinct dockets this organization string commented on, across every agency and year. Repeats on each committee row of the string.
columns.first_comment_date: Earliest `posted_date` across this organization's comments in every agency and year (ISO 8601 string).
columns.last_comment_date: Latest `posted_date` across this organization's comments in every agency and year (ISO 8601 string).
columns.connected_organization_name: The committee's connected organization (its sponsor) as FEC states it, verbatim from `fec_committee_history.connected_organization_name` in the latest filing year that names one. NULL when no year names one: FEC's placeholders (`NONE`, `N/A`, `NA`, `BLANK`, `0`, punctuation alone), which that table keeps verbatim, are read as naming none. Filers sometimes write the PAC's own name, a former name or a parent company here.
columns.sponsor_name_match: Whether `connected_organization_name` names the commenting organization: `agrees` when it reduces to `organization_core` under the same normalization (read also with PAC words such as `POLITICAL ACTION COMMITTEE` removed, spaces ignored); `differs` otherwise, most often the same organization spelled another way (`ASSN`, inverted words, a typo), a former name or a parent company, sometimes a different sponsor; `not_stated` when FEC names no sponsor. A name comparison, not an identity.
columns.agency_codes: Native list of the distinct agency codes this organization commented to, across every year, sorted. Repeats on each committee row of the string. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.association_kind: Meaning of the stated organization-to-committee association; no shared legal identity is implied.

columns.release_id: Digest of the chamber and the item's full link; replaces a truncated-URL unique key.
columns.chamber: Which committee feed this item came from.
columns.title: The item title in full, never truncated to a display length.
columns.guid: The item's guid, where it carries one.
columns.guid_is_permalink: The guid's isPermaLink, defaulting to true when the attribute is absent.
columns.description: The item's raw HTML description exactly as the publisher wrote it, untruncated.
columns.description_text: That description read as plain text, not a truncated excerpt.
columns.pub_date: The item's pubDate exactly as the publisher spelled it, wrong zone abbreviation included.
columns.pub_date_instant: That pubDate parsed to an instant under RFC 822's fixed abbreviation table.  A zone label is taken at its word: the Senate feed stamps `EST` all year, so a summer release reads -05:00, an hour off its clock time.
columns.author: The item's author, which the Senate feed states as a shared mailbox.
columns.creator: The item's dc:creator, which the House feed states as a named staffer.
columns.categories: Every category the item lists, as a Native list. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.enclosure_url: The enclosure URL, where the item carries one.
columns.enclosure_length: The enclosure length in bytes, where the item states one.
columns.enclosure_type: The enclosure media type, where the item states one.
columns.bill_id: The bill this release names, where a bill-number pattern matched.

columns.proceeding_id: Stable opaque id of the proceeding (`proceeding_<24 hex>`), continued from the prior generation where it overlaps one.
columns.rin: The proceeding's RIN when it holds exactly one, else NULL; a query aid, never its identity (`rins` lists every RIN).
columns.docket_ids: Native list of the Regulations.gov dockets the proceeding comprises; `[]` for a docket-less proceeding. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.title: Title of its most recently dated titled document.
columns.agency_code: The agency code most of its documents carry. A docket-less proceeding takes its Register document's agency code. Each Register agency maps to one Regulations.gov code through RefSpec's agency projection and agency registry, whose identity bridges and successions give a defunct agency its current successor's code whatever the document's date: a 1998 Health Care Finance Administration notice is CMS. A split agency maps only when every successor gives the same one code. A department named with one of its own agencies yields to it (Transportation Department with FAA is FAA), and a department signing with one of its own unmapped bureaus keeps the department's code. NULL when no agency maps or the agencies are unrelated.
columns.current_stage: The one stage (`proposed`, `supplemental`, `final` or `withdrawn`) of its latest dated events; NULL when none, or when that day's events disagree.
columns.stage_events: Native list of its stage events, one per staged document: `{effective_date, event_kind, evidence_id, joined_by, source, stage}`. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.fr_document_numbers: Native list of the Federal Register document numbers it holds. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.cfr_refs: Native list of the CFR references (`title-part`) that the `rule_targets` edges of its dockets name. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.cfr_target_iris: The same CFR references as Rulespec identifiers (e.g. `urn:rkaf:us:cfr:40:60`). Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.authority_refs: Always `[]`: legal authority belongs to the editioned Unified Agenda entry, never to an action. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.fr_document_ids: Native list of the dated Federal Register record ids (`number@YYYY-MM-DD`) it holds. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.rins: Native list of every RIN it holds, from its dockets, documents and Register documents. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.fr_document_joins_json: How each `fr_document_ids` document joined, in the same order: `{fr_document_id, joined_by}`, `joined_by` being `fr_docket_link`, `fr_copy`, `specific_rin` or `fr_document`.
columns.unresolved_fr_references_json: JSON array of Register number references it holds that resolve to no single record, each with its candidates and status.

columns.bill_id: The bill this event is about.
columns.event_type: One of the four sealed event types.
columns.subject_id: The version or summary key the event is about, unit-separator joined; empty for a bill event.
columns.occurred_at: The publisher's own instant for the change, falling back to the run instant.
columns.title: The few fields a reader needs to render the event without joining another table. This column retains the source property title.
columns.stage: The few fields a reader needs to render the event without joining another table. This column retains the source property stage.
columns.sponsor_bioguide_id: The few fields a reader needs to render the event without joining another table. This column retains the source property sponsor_bioguide_id.
columns.from_stage: The few fields a reader needs to render the event without joining another table. This column retains the source property from.
columns.to_stage: The few fields a reader needs to render the event without joining another table. This column retains the source property to.
columns.version_code: The few fields a reader needs to render the event without joining another table. This column retains the source property version_code.
columns.kind: The few fields a reader needs to render the event without joining another table. This column retains the source property kind.

columns.issue: The issue number within that volume, as the publisher spells it.
columns.congress: The numbered Congress the issue belongs to.
columns.session: The session of Congress the issue belongs to.
columns.issue_date: The issue date instant as the publisher states it.
columns.chambers: Which chambers this issue records a sitting of, unit-separator joined and sorted (`house`, `senate`); NULL where sections is NULL, empty where the detail names no chamber section. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.section_count: How many sections the detail lists; NULL where sections is NULL.
columns.section_names: Every section name the detail lists, unit-separator joined, in publisher order; NULL where sections is NULL. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.sections: Every section the detail lists, as a Native list of the publisher's objects. NULL where no detail was read or the detail states no such list; `[]` where it states an empty one. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.entire_issue: Every whole-issue rendition the detail lists, as a Native list of the publisher's objects. NULL where no detail was read or the detail states no such list; `[]` where it states an empty one. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.package_id: The GovInfo CREC package id read from the file stem of the whole-issue link for part 1. NULL where the detail lists no part 1, or part 1 links under two stems.
columns.article_count: How many articles the detail says the issue has.
columns.update_date: The publisher's updateDate; the merge prefers the larger value.

columns.rin: The Regulation Identifier Number the item is (e.g. `2060-AV16`).
columns.scope_status: `recurring` (its latest Agenda priority is Routine and Frequent), `single_observed` (evidence links one proceeding) or `unresolved` (none or several).
columns.linked_proceeding_count: How many proceedings `agenda_item_proceedings` links the item to, as a decimal string.
columns.observation_count: How many distinct Unified Agenda entries (edition and URL) list the RIN, as a decimal string; `0` when no edition does.
columns.latest_agenda_edition: The latest Unified Agenda edition listing the RIN, `YYYYMM`; NULL when no edition does.
columns.first_seen: Earliest Eastern day any source dates the RIN: an Agenda edition or action date, a docket or document date, or a Register publication.
columns.last_seen: Latest Eastern day any source dates the RIN.
columns.unresolved_fr_references_json: JSON array of unresolved Register number references from the Register documents that state this RIN.

columns.package_id: The report package this block was parsed from.
columns.seq: Zero-based position of this block in its part, in reading order.
columns.body: The block's text, trimmed the way the original trimmed it.
columns.char_start: Start offset of this block's span in the flattened report text.
columns.char_end: End offset, exclusive; spans partition the whole input with no gap and no overlap.
columns.body_chars: Character length of body, which can be shorter than the span it sits in.
columns.last_modified: The parent report's last_modified, carried so this table versions with the package it came from.
columns.heading: The source heading as spelled and trimmed, including actual agency names and generic titles; NULL for preamble or full_report blocks, which have no source heading.
columns.part_id: The report part this block was parsed from, spelled as `committee_reports.part_id`, so (package_id, part_id, last_modified) is the parent row.  Appended last.

columns.vote_id: Natural key: congress, chamber, session and roll number joined with hyphens.
columns.congress: The numbered Congress the roll call belongs to.
columns.session: The session number within that Congress.
columns.roll_number: The roll-call number within that session.
columns.vote_date: The chamber's literal date; sorts as text, not by time (see `vote_day`).
columns.question: The question put to the chamber, as the publisher states it.
columns.result: The stated result of the roll call.
columns.yea: Yea votes, from the Clerk's yea-total or the Senate's yeas; a blank Senate count reads 0 (see present).
columns.nay: Nay votes, from the Clerk's nay-total or the Senate's nays; a blank Senate count reads 0 (see present).
columns.present: Present votes, as each publisher counts them. A Senate count element the file leaves empty or omits (`<present/>`) reads 0, which is what the Senate means by it: 119-senate-1-15 states 50 yeas, 50 nays and empty present and absent, 100 positions.
columns.not_voting: Members not voting: the Clerk's not-voting-total, or the Senate's absent, folded to one column. A blank Senate `<absent/>` reads 0, as for present.
columns.tallies: The overall totals the publisher stated, under the publisher's own names, as a Native structure; the Clerk's totals by party are party_totals. Candidate elections keep literal choice labels here and leave the four ordinary tally columns NULL. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.member_vote_count: How many member positions the file carried; the member_votes row count for this roll call.
columns.bill_id: The bill this roll call refers to: from a bill action's recorded-vote reference, a vote-list reference, or the vote file's own statement of its measure.
columns.tally_kind: positions for ordinary totals, candidates for native named-choice totals; NULL on legacy or linkage-only rows.
columns.documents: Ordered Senate document objects with native congress, type, number, nomination_id, name, title and short_title; [] for captured votes without documents, NULL for legacy or linkage-only rows. Numbers retain publisher spelling, including nomination suffixes; nomination_id carries {congress}-pn-{number}[-{part}] on PN documents and NULL otherwise. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.amendments: Ordered Senate amendment objects with native number, to_amendment_number, to_amendment_to_amendment_number, to_document_number, to_document_short_title and purpose; [] for captured votes without amendments, NULL for legacy or linkage-only rows. Repeated empty-ID blocks remain separate observations; no document pairing is inferred. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.vote_day: The chamber's own printed vote date as an ISO day (YYYY-MM-DD) in Eastern local time, which sorts where vote_date does not and is never the UTC day of a Congress.gov recordedVotes date; NULL where the file prints no date, on linkage-only rows, and on rows published before this column until a host backfills them.
columns.legis_num: The Clerk's own legis-num as the House vote file states it (H R 3354, H RES 682, QUORUM); empty when a captured Clerk file states none; NULL on Senate rows, linkage-only rows and House rows captured before this column.
columns.clerk_body_element: Which element of the Clerk's file names the voting body, `committee` or `chamber`; both read 'U.S. House of Representatives', so the element is the fact.  The Clerk files 3,830 of its 22,512 roll calls of 1990-2026 under <committee>, all from 2007 on: 3,791 amendment votes, 29 motions for the committee to rise or calls in committee, 5 rulings of the chair, 3 vacated votes and 2 House questions (a passage, a recommittal).  It calls none a Committee of the Whole vote; that is the inference.  NULL on Senate rows, linkage-only rows and rows captured before this column.
columns.vote_desc: The Clerk's own vote-desc as the House vote file states it, most often the measure's title ("PRECIP Act"); 13,780 of the Clerk's 22,512 files of 1990-2026 state one.  On the five roll calls the House vacated by unanimous consent before recording a position (112-1-484, 112-2-327, 113-2-275, 114-1-300, 114-2-44) it is the file's statement of what happened ("This vote was vacated by unanimous consent on 4-Jun-2015."), and the row has zero tallies, member_vote_count 0 and no member_votes rows.  A vote vacated after its positions were recorded publishes as any other: 110-2-640 (2008) lists 433 members and says "Proceedings on Roll Call 640 were vacated by unanimous consent."  Empty when a captured Clerk file states none; NULL on Senate rows, linkage-only rows and House rows captured before this column.
columns.vote_question_text: The Senate's full question text as the file states it, the amendment and the measure named in words (On the Amendment S.Amdt. 2360 to H.R. 1), so it names the amendment voted on even when the amendment block is empty (119-2-180 and 119-2-182 name SA 5823 only here and in vote_title). Empty when a captured Senate file states none; NULL on House rows, linkage-only rows and Senate rows captured before this column.
columns.vote_title: The Senate's vote title as the file states it (`Amdt. No. 2360, as Amended`). Empty when a captured Senate file states none; NULL on House rows, linkage-only rows and Senate rows captured before this column.
columns.majority_requirement: The majority the Senate file states the question needed: `1/2`, `3/5` or `2/3`. Empty when a captured Senate file states none; NULL on House rows, linkage-only rows and Senate rows captured before this column.
columns.modify_date: The Senate file's own modify_date literal (`July 1, 2025,  12:57 PM`), when the publisher last changed it; sorts as text. Empty when a captured Senate file states none; NULL on House rows, linkage-only rows and Senate rows captured before this column.
columns.tie_breaker_by_whom: Who cast the tie-breaking vote, as the Senate's tie_breaker block names them (`Vice President of the United States`): the reason a 50-50 roll call reads Agreed to. NULL when the vote was not tied (the block is present and empty), on House rows, linkage-only rows and Senate rows captured before this column.
columns.tie_breaker_vote: The tie-breaking vote as cast (`Yea`); NULL wherever tie_breaker_by_whom is.
columns.party_totals: The Clerk's totals by party, as a Native list in the file's order: each object the party as the Clerk names it (Republican, Democratic, Independent; member_votes.party spells the same parties R, D and I) and its yea-total, nay-total, present-total and not-voting-total. [] when a captured Clerk file states none (a Speaker election). NULL on Senate rows, whose files state none; on linkage-only rows; and on House rows captured before this column until they are read again. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.source_url: The publisher's own URL for this roll call.
columns.match_rule: Which vote-matching rule named that bill: bill_action_recorded_vote (the bill's own action records this roll call), house_vote_legislation (Congress.gov's House vote list), vote_file_legislation (the vote file names the bill: the Clerk's legis-num, or the Senate's document or amended document), or unmatched.
columns.match_action_index: Position of the action whose recordedVote named this roll call, where one did.
columns.match_url: The reference URL the match was read from.
columns.conflict_count: How many later references disagreed with the one that won; kept, never dropped.

columns.rule_target_id: Stable identity of this rule-target assertion, preserving repeated observations independently.
columns.docket_id: Regulations.gov docket the edge belongs to, normalized; joins `dockets.docket_id`.
columns.cfr_ref: CFR reference the rule targets, `title-part` or `title-part.section` (e.g. `40-60`); NULL on a RIN-only or citation edge.
columns.cfr_section: The CFR section of `cfr_ref` when it names one; NULL for a part-level reference.
columns.rin: Regulation Identifier Number the edge carries (e.g. `2060-AV16`); NULL on a CFR-only or citation edge.
columns.first_seen: Earliest Eastern day any evidence for the edge is dated, `YYYY-MM-DD`.
columns.last_seen: Latest Eastern day any evidence for the edge is dated, `YYYY-MM-DD`.
columns.fr_document_ids: Dated Federal Register document identities associated with this subject; no applicability inference is implied. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.evidence_id: The least id of the records stating the edge: the docket for `docket_rin`, a dated Register record id (`number@YYYY-MM-DD`) for `fr_cfr_ref`, else a Regulations.gov document id.
columns.fr_references_json: JSON array of the literal Federal Register number references behind the edge, each with the `status` saying how it resolved (`dated`, `single_candidate_in_input`, `ambiguous`, `missing`, or a folded or unpadded match).

columns.proceeding_id: The docketed proceeding the lifecycle reads; joins `proceedings.proceeding_id`.
columns.kind: What its events make: `finalized` (a final strictly after the proposal), `companion` (a Register-dated final on the proposal's Register day, 54b; no survival outcome), `upload_pair` (an upload-dated proposal and a final that day, 54c; no survival outcome), `withdrawn` (a Register or Agenda withdrawal on or after the proposal, no later final), `open` (censored at `censor_date`), `final_without_observed_proposal` or `no_anchor`.
columns.proposal_date: Day of the earliest proposed event; NULL without a proposal.
columns.proposal_document_id: The proposal's document: a dated Register record id (`number@YYYY-MM-DD`) when the Register dates a proposal of the proceeding, else a Regulations.gov document id (decision 54d).
columns.proposal_form: The proposal's form from its title: `proposed`, `advance_proposed`, `comment_period` or `correction`.
columns.final_date: Day of the final the lifecycle pairs or anchors on; NULL without one.
columns.final_document_id: The final's document, spelled as `proposal_document_id` is.
columns.final_form: The final's form from its title: `final`, `interim_final`, `direct_final` or `correction`.
columns.finals_before_proposal: Finals dated before the proposal, counted and never paired; NULL without a proposal.
columns.withdrawal_date: Day of the withdrawal that makes it `withdrawn`; NULL otherwise.
columns.withdrawal_document_id: The withdrawal: a dated Register record id, or the agenda item id (`urn:rkaf:us:rin:<rin>`) of an Agenda withdrawal.
columns.outcome: Its survival outcome: `final`, `withdrawn` (a competing outcome) or `censored`; NULL for a kind outside survival.
columns.duration_days: Days from the proposal to the final, the withdrawal or `censor_date`; NULL without an outcome.
columns.censor_date: The generation's last event day, capped at the run's day, where open lifecycles are censored; one date in every row.
columns.open_signal: What the latest Unified Agenda entry of its specific RINs says (`agenda_completed_final`, `agenda_completed_withdrawn`, `agenda_completed_other`, `agenda_long_term`, `agenda_active`, `agenda_dropped_off`), else `not_on_agenda` or `no_specific_rin`.
columns.routine_family: The routine family the proposal's own title names (the final's without a proposal; the proceeding's with no anchor), read at time zero so the stratum never depends on the outcome (decision 55a): `airworthiness_directive`, `airspace`, `state_air_plan`, `pesticide_tolerance` (pesticide-petition receipts included), `coast_guard_local`; NULL otherwise.
columns.agenda_priority: That Agenda entry's `priority_category` (e.g. `Economically Significant`); NULL without one.
columns.agenda_major: That Agenda entry's `major` (`Yes`, `No` or `Undetermined`); NULL without one.
columns.specific_rins: Native list of the RINs the proceeding's docket-side evidence alone holds. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.pre_2008_coverage: Whether it is anchored before 2008, when Regulations.gov coverage is thin; NULL without an anchor, or for an upload pair from 2008 on.

columns.uei: Unique Entity ID (SAM `ueiSAM`, 12-char alphanumeric, e.g. `Q93HWX24PGA4`). With `entity_eft_indicator`, the registration key; alone, the entity-resolution join key.
columns.entity_eft_indicator: SAM `entityEFTIndicator`: which of an entity's registrations this is, one per EFT (bank-account) indicator. NULL for an entity's sole registration.
columns.cage_code: Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code assigned to the entity. Often null for newly registered entities.
columns.legal_business_name: Legal business name as registered in SAM.gov.
columns.dba_name: 'Doing business as' name, when the entity registered one. Often null.
columns.entity_structure_desc: Entity structure description (`coreData.generalInformation.entityStructureDesc`, e.g. `Corporate Entity (Not Tax Exempt)`).
columns.state: State or province code of the physical address (`coreData.physicalAddress.stateOrProvinceCode`). Null for many non-US registrants.
columns.zip_code: ZIP / postal code of the physical address.
columns.congressional_district: U.S. congressional district of the physical address (`coreData.congressionalDistrict`). Null for non-US registrants.
columns.primary_naics: Primary NAICS industry code the entity asserted (`assertions.goodsAndServices.primaryNaics`). Often null.
columns.registration_status: Always `Active` here: the ingest asks SAM for active registrations (`registrationStatus=A`) and replaces a year's rows only when it re-reads that year, so a row is active as of its year's last read, not today; compare `registration_expiration_date` with the query date.
columns.registration_date: Date the entity's current registration was recorded (ISO 8601 string).
columns.registration_expiration_date: Date the current registration expires (ISO 8601 string).
columns.exclusion_status_flag: Whether the entity has an active exclusion/debarment record (`Y`/`N`).
columns.entity_url: Entity's self-reported website URL (`coreData.entityInformation.entityURL`). Often null.

columns.scorecard_id: Stable publisher edition identifier; join within the recorded source snapshot.
columns.item_id: Unchanged publisher scoring-item key within the edition.
columns.reference_id: Derived occurrence key: item:direct or reference: followed by the source occurrence identifier.

columns.chamber: Exactly resolved chamber; NULL when not established.

columns.package_id: The GovInfo package id the page belongs to, `GPO-CDOC-119sdoc3`.  Not unique on its own: one package publishes the whole report and each of its parts as separate PDFs, so `file_name` is in the identity beside it.
columns.file_name: Which PDF of that package this page is in, `GPO-CDOC-119sdoc3-1.pdf`.  Part of the identity because the package's two files, `Part I` (-1.pdf) and `Part II` (-2.pdf) as its MODS titles them, open with the same printed pages -- measured byte-identical extracted text over the first 60 pages of GPO-CDOC-119sdoc3 -- before Part II goes on to its own half of the B- statement, and keying on the package alone would collide them.
columns.page: The one-based PDF page the table was found on, as the extraction states it.
columns.table_ordinal: Which table on that page, zero-based, in the order the extraction returned them.  Measured 139 of 139 pages carry exactly one, so this is `0` throughout the sample and exists because nothing in the print guarantees it.
columns.row_ordinal: Which ruled row of that table, zero-based, top to bottom.
columns.body_version_id: Digest of the page text this row's context was read from, and part of the identity.  A page, table and row ordinal mean nothing without it: a re-extraction that finds one more ruled band moves every ordinal after it, and keying on the digest is what stops two extractions of one page from colliding on one identity and silently merging.  It pins the text, not the table finder, so a change in the table finder alone is not visible here.
columns.printed_page: The print's own page label, the last non-empty line of the page text: `A-7`, `B-1243`, `x`.  Present on 139 of 139 measured table pages.  This is the locator the volume's table of contents indexes by; the PDF page number is not.
columns.section_heading: The section heading the page states, one of `SUMMARY OF TRANSACTIONS BY APPROPRIATIONS` or `DETAILED AND SUMMARY STATEMENT OF EXPENDITURES`.  NULL on a continuation page, which repeats neither.
columns.grid_kind: Which of the print's three ruled grids this table is, decided by the label its own first row states: `appropriation_summary`, `organization_detail` or `payee_detail`.  NULL where the first row states none of the three, so an unrecognised grid is visible rather than mislabelled.
columns.row_kind: What the print makes this row: `header` where at least two of its cells are header labels, `total` where it is the grid's own `Totals` row or carries `ORGANIZATION TOTALS`, `entry` otherwise.
columns.cells_ruled: Whether the print rules this row into more than one cell.  `true` on every `appropriation_summary` body row (nine cells of nine) and `false` on every `organization_detail` and `payee_detail` entry row (one of ten, one of seven), so `WHERE cells_ruled` selects exactly the rows whose cells are separate facts rather than one block of text.
columns.office: The office or account the page names between its section heading and its `Funding Year` line, `SENATOR TIM KAINE`; a label the print wraps over two lines is joined with one space (`CHAIRMAN MAJORITY POLICY COMMITTEE (D)`, printed with `(D)` on its own line), so the Majority and Minority Conference chairs are not both `COMMITTEE (D)`.  NULL on a continuation page, which the print leaves unlabelled; a consumer forward-fills in `printed_page` order.
columns.funding_year: The funding year the page's own `Funding Year` line states, and the **first** of them where it states a span, so a single-year block and a multi-year appropriation are comparable on this column. The no-year or revolving marker remains `X`, and compact numeric labels remain literal. NULL where the page states no funding-year line, which is every continuation page.
columns.funding_year_end: The last year of a multi-year appropriation, which the print spells `Funding Year 2021-2023` and its own contents spell `FY 21/23`.  NULL where the print states one year, so a span and a single year are told apart rather than folded together.  Five of the 83 measured office pages are spans -- the Chaplain's, printed B-48 to B-55.
columns.appropriation_title: The appropriation the page names under its funding year, joined to one line; the module docstring quotes one in full.  NULL where the page states none.
columns.period_start: The first day of the period the table's own column headers state, as ISO `2024-10-01`.  Read from `FUNDS AVAILABLE AS OF October 1, 2024` or from the first date of a `PERIOD OF` header, the only two spellings measured; NULL where no header states one, which is every `payee_detail` table.
columns.period_end: The last day of that period, as ISO `2025-03-31`, from `UNEXPENDED BALANCE AS OF March 31, 2025` or from the same header's second date.  NULL on the same terms as `period_start`.
columns.column_headers: One entry per column: the header label governing this row at that index, whitespace collapsed and exactly as the print spells it, or null where the band names none.  The band is the nearest run of header rows above this one, which is what makes the role correct in an `organization_detail` table -- it carries two bands, and column 0 goes from the office block to `DOCUMENT NO.` partway down. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.cells: One entry per column: the cell exactly as the print states it, newlines and all, or null where the extraction found no cell region there.  This is the row; every other content column is a promotion out of it and none replaces it. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.account_title: The cell whose governing header is `APPROPRIATION TITLE`, which carries the account name with its fiscal years stacked under it, or `Totals` on the section's own total row.  Filled only where `cells_ruled`, so it is never a blob cell read as a title.
columns.account_number: The cell whose governing header is `NO.`, the Senate's four-digit appropriation account number (`0100`, `4046`).  Filled on the same terms as `account_title`; the print states it empty on the `Totals` row.
columns.amounts: One entry per column: null where the cell states no amount, otherwise every line of that cell that parses, in printed order, as objects carrying the exact printed line and its decimal.  A money cell stacks one amount per fiscal year, which is why this is a list and not a scalar, and a line that does not parse is not here and stands unchanged in `cells`. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.amount_count: How many amounts this row states across every column; `0` where it states none.
columns.table_row_count: How many ruled rows the table this row belongs to has.
columns.table_column_count: How many ruled columns it has.  Measured 7, 9 and 10 across the sample, one value per grid kind.

T.` (revised title) or a Revised Statutes or Internal Revenue Code reference (`R.S. Sec 572`). NULL where it prints none. columns.usc_section_key: The one U.S. Code section the row names, as a join key: the section number without Table III's printed note words (`nt`, `nts`, `prec.`; usc_place states them), lower-cased, with every dash spelling an ASCII hyphen, as RefSpec's section oracle keys it. columns.agenda_edition: Semiannual agenda edition the row was published in, as reginfo.gov's `pubId` `YYYYMM`: MM 04 and 10 are its spring and fall editions, except that reginfo.gov titles 202510 the "2026" agenda (202504 is Spring 2025). The month is not a release date: an edition appears months later (USDA printed 202510 in the Register on 2026-08-14), and no release date is held. Half of the primary/dedup key. Every readable edition since 199510 is held, so filter to one edition, or count distinct `rin`, before counting rules.
columns.major: Whether the action is a major rule, as reported by the agenda (e.g. `Yes`/`No`). Often null.
columns.publication_id: reginfo.gov publication identifier for this agenda entry, when present.
columns.timetable: Native list of planned and actual milestone actions with literal source dates and Federal Register citations. A date with day 00 has month precision; labels such as To Be Determined remain unchanged. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.cfr_references: Native list of CFR citations affected by the rulemaking. The join key to the CFR. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.legal_authority: Native list of legal-authority citations the agency cites for the rulemaking. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.first_action_date: Earliest distinct calendar date derived from the timetable within years 1900–2100, or NULL when none is derivable. Source month-only dates (MM/00/YYYY) use day 01 here, and out-of-range sentinel or typo years are excluded; timetable retains literal source dates.
columns.next_action_date: Second distinct calendar date derived from the timetable within years 1900–2100, or NULL when fewer than two dates are derivable. May be historical; it is not selected relative to today. Source month-only dates use day 01 here, and out-of-range sentinel or typo years are excluded; timetable retains literal source dates.
columns.related_rins: Native list of the RINs the publisher lists as related to this entry, each a (`rin`, `rin_relation`) pair in source order; a RIN listed twice keeps both positions. Values are stripped of leading and trailing whitespace while internal whitespace is preserved verbatim, and otherwise kept as written: no RIN shape is checked, so self-references, malformed values such as `d as AF61` and the cut-off relations `Related t` and `Previously report` remain. The publisher documents `Merge with` but writes `Merged with`. NULL means the row states no related-RIN list only in a generation replayed from every retained edition; a row restored from a regulations-native-v1 generation, which predates this column, is also NULL because it was never read. Incremental builds re-read such editions through the bounded backfill (60 per run, covering the full series in a single run), so that ambiguity lasts only until every held edition has been read once, except for a restored row the re-read no longer lists, which stays NULL. `agenda_related_rins` resolves each pair against held agenda rows. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.legal_deadlines: Native list of statutory or judicial deadlines listed in the agenda entry's `LEGAL_DLINE_LIST`, each with `dline_type`, `dline_action_stage`, `dline_date`, and `dline_desc` in source order (edge-stripped, internal whitespace and literal values such as `nulldate` preserved). NULL when the edition states no legal-deadline list or predates reading it; `[]` when the list container is explicitly empty. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.parent_rin: Parent Regulation Identifier Number stated in `PARENT_RIN` (edge-stripped, verbatim otherwise), or NULL when absent or unread.
columns.child_rins: Native list of child Regulation Identifier Numbers stated in `CHILD_RIN_LIST` in source order (edge-stripped, blank entries omitted, duplicates preserved). NULL when the edition states no child-RIN list or predates reading it; `[]` when the list container is explicitly empty. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
